functions.sandbox/interaction_engine.py::GraphSamp: Neighbour selection over a fixed Watts-Strogatz graph, built once at construction from graph_seed alone and never per turn. Maps node indices to agent IDs positionally and caches each agent's sorted graph neighbours. Uses connected_watts_strogatz_graph so rewiring cannot leave a disconnected population.

Validates degree (even, at least 2, under the population size), rewire_p in [0,1], k (at least 1, no more than degree) and that agent_ids are unique, raising ValueError on each rather than coercing. Then builds the connected WS graph, rejects it if any node came out short of k neighbours, and caches agent_id to sorted-neighbour-list. Sorting makes the later sample a function of the seed rather than of networkx's adjacency order.

Samples k distinct graph neighbours of speaker without replacement, consuming rng exactly once, and returns them as Agent objects in sampled order because delivery order is part of the stimulus. Raises if the speaker is not a graph node, if it has fewer than k neighbours (a case the constructor's check already rejects) or if a chosen neighbour is absent from all_agents. turn is unused: the graph does not change over the run.
The edge list as sorted (agent_id, agent_id) pairs. Exposed so analysis can compute assortativity over the structure the run actually used rather than a graph rebuilt afterwards.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::ModelGateway.s: The probe call: one token at temperature 0 with the top logprobs attached, returned on BackendResponse.top_logprobs. Takes the same concurrency slot and rate-limiter lease as generate and records the cost as text modality, because a probe is a billed request against the same server and the bank regime makes two calls per agent per round. max_tokens=1 and temperature=0 are fixed here, not passed in.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::ModelGateway._: One litellm.acompletion with logprobs=True and top_logprobs set from construction, retried up to three times with exponential backoff on TransientGatewayError. Maps rate-limit and connection errors to transient, authentication and bad-request errors to FatalGatewayError, and a context-window overflow to ContextLengthExceeded, caught first because it subclasses BadRequestError. BadRequestError otherwise covers a server with no logprobs support, which is fatal because retrying cannot make a server grow the feature.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::_extract_top_l: Walks choices[0].logprobs.content[0].top_logprobs and returns [(token, logprob), ...] as str and float. Raises FatalGatewayError at every missing level rather than returning an empty list, so a server that never returns logprobs surfaces as one loud failure instead of a per-agent scoring failure on every round. Reads both attribute-style objects and plain dicts.
Builds the FatalGatewayError for one missing level, naming the model, the detail, and that the server must support logprobs/top_logprobs.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::_first_token_t: The sampled token's text from choices[0].message.content, or an empty string when absent. Not used for scoring, which reads the distribution; kept so a probe row records what the model actually emitted.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::_get: Reads name off obj as a dict key when obj is a dict, else as an attribute, returning None if absent. Lets the logprob walk handle both shapes litellm produces.
functions.sandbox/models.py::Interaction.check_nei: Requires at least one neighbor_agent_id for generated_text and meme rows, preserving what the original Field(min_length=1) protected after that constraint was relaxed. Bank rows are exempt because the round-0 probe genuinely has no neighbours.
functions.sandbox/models.py::Interaction.check_pro: Rejects a probe_dist that is not exactly seven values. A different length means the scorer renormalized over a different support than probe_mean was computed on, so the two columns would disagree.
functions.sandbox/models.py::ExperimentRun.check_g: Rejects an odd graph_degree unconditionally, since the Watts-Strogatz ring connects degree/2 neighbours per side. Only when neighbor_strategy is "graph" does it also require degree < M and N <= degree, so the default degree of 6 does not reject small-population alpha configs over a field they never read.
functions.sandbox/models.py::ExperimentRun.check_b: For regime="bank", requires both bank_path and probe_question to be set and non-blank, naming whichever is missing. Neither is defaulted: a generic English probe_question would silently probe every language arm in English.
functions.sandbox/probe_scorer.py::ProbeMassTooLow: Raised when the share of next-token probability on the digits 1-7 fell below the configured floor. Carries the observed mass and the floor so a caller can log how far short it fell. A refusal to measure, not a value to repair.
Stores mass and mass_floor on the exception and builds a message quoting both to four decimal places.
functions.sandbox/probe_scorer.py::ProbeScore: One probe read, frozen. mean is the expected scale point and is the stance value; dist is the seven probabilities renormalized to sum to 1; mass is the share of the raw next-token distribution that was on the digits, before renormalizing; side_conf is how concentrated the read is on the side the mean falls on.
functions.sandbox/probe_scorer.py::score: Reads a stance from [(token, logprob), ...]. Exponentiates each logprob, sums probability per scale point after stripping whitespace so "3" and " 3" count as one answer, and divides by the on-scale mass to get dist and mean. Raises ValueError for a mass_floor outside (0, 1] or an empty input list, and ProbeMassTooLow when the on-scale mass is under the floor. The total probability seen across all tokens is computed but deliberately not returned.
functions.sandbox/probe_scorer.py::_side_confidenc: Sums the renormalized probability above the midpoint when mean is above it, below it when mean is below, and returns P(s = 4) when mean is exactly the midpoint. Separates how decided a read is from where it stands: a distribution split between 1 and 7 and one piled on 4 both have mean 4.
functions.sandbox/prompt_builder.py::RoundMemory: One past round as the agent experienced it: the bank text of the posts it read, already rendered in the language it saw them in, and the reply it wrote. The builder never looks text up, so the orchestrator decides the rendering. Empty in both fields is a round whose reply failed and left no memory slot; every applied round has something in posts_read, the delivery: off control included, since its agents read one side-free message.
functions.sandbox/prompt_builder.py::PromptBuilder: The original generated-regime prompt, unchanged: position, memory, neighbour posts, topic, language directive and the STANCE output contract, with an image attached when a meme neighbour's post has one and vision is available. Returns a BuiltPrompt recording whether the vision fallback was used.

The bank-regime reply prompt: persona, topic, the lean sentence, memory of past rounds, the feed of delivered bank texts, the language directive, and an instruction to reply in one or two sentences. The lean sits directly after the topic line in every round, not round 1 alone, because it states a permanent trait and a sentence that vanishes makes consecutive rounds two different instruments. Omits the memory and feed sections entirely when empty. Never attaches an image and never states a position number or an agent id.

The probe prompt, as plain text rather than a BuiltPrompt. A fresh context holding persona, topic, the lean sentence, the same memory the reply prompt showed, the run's survey question, the two anchor labels against 1 and 7, and an instruction to answer with a single digit. The lean is unconditional, as in the reply prompt: showing it at round 0 and withholding it afterwards would make the step between the first two readings partly measure the removal of a sentence, and under delivery: off it was the only thing that changed between rounds at all.

Returns run.probe_question, raising if it is unset or blank. Unreachable through the loader, which already requires it; kept because a default English fallback would probe all four arms in English and leave no trace in the output.

The agent's starting position stated in words, from LEAN_SENTENCES keyed by initial_stance as an integer and formatted against the run's own anchor labels, which are English in every arm because the sentence around them is. Rendered into every bank reply prompt and every probe prompt. Raises for a non-integer or out-of-range stance rather than rounding or defaulting to undecided, since the probe reads exactly the seven scale points.

Renders the agent's past rounds oldest first as "You read:" and "You replied:" lines, with rounds separated by a rule and no round numbers or agent ids. Renders the whole history when memory_rounds is None, the default, and only the last memory_rounds rounds when a run configures a window; nothing is dropped silently, an over-long prompt being max_prompt_tokens' business. Returns an empty string when there is nothing to show, so the caller omits the section.
Returns run.memory_rounds as given, None included. No fallback default, because one would turn "keep the full history" into a window nobody asked for.

Renders each delivered bank text as an "A user posted:" line under one heading. No agent id, which would be a handle an agent could track across rounds and turn a feed of arguments into a feed of sources. Returns an empty string for an empty feed so the heading is omitted rather than left bare; no bank round reaches it empty now that the control delivers a neutral message, so it guards the probe path and future callers.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager.gra: The integer seed for the run's Watts-Strogatz graph, base_seed + 9000003. A plain int because networkx builds its own generator and the graph is constructed once, so there is no stream to advance or checkpoint. Offset far from every other stream, and a function of the base seed alone, so two runs differing only in language share a graph.
functions.sandbox/seed_manager.py::SeedManager.sen: A stream for one (purpose, sender) with no turn in the derivation, seeded from the string f"{seed}|{purpose}|{sender_id}". Exists for the argument bank, whose no-repeat guarantee needs the draw to depend on how many times a sender has posted rather than on which turn it is. Keyed by string because Random hashes it through SHA-512, stable across processes where hash(agent_id) is not. Raises for an unknown purpose or an empty sender_id.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::Simu: True when run.regime is "bank". The single branch point between the two per-turn loops.

One turn of the original loop, in the order Fix F requires: freeze the snapshot, resolve every agent's neighbours, resolve which scheduled speakers post a meme, then dispatch all M agents concurrently with return_exceptions=True. Meme speakers take a free dataset lookup instead of an LLM call. Writes one Interaction per agent, then applies the valid ones and advances last posts.

One bank round. Resolves each agent's side, the item it posts, its neighbours and what it is delivered, all before any dispatch; then gathers Phase A (every reply) and Phase B (every probe, each seeing this round's own reply) concurrently. Under delivery: off each agent is delivered the run's neutral message under the reserved item id instead of its neighbours' items, and Phase A still runs, so the control makes the same reply calls and every seeded stream advances identically to a treatment arm. Writes one row per agent, advances the bank cycle for everyone, and applies only the rows valid for analysis.

Probes every agent once before anything is read, so the starting stance is a measurement in the dataset rather than initial_stance, which the config chose. The prompt is the instrument every later probe uses minus the history it does not have yet, the lean sentence included, so the step from this reading to round 1's measures what the agent read rather than a change in the question. Writes one turn-0 row per agent with no neighbours, no posted item and no reply.

pro above the scale midpoint, con below, and a seeded draw exactly on it. Takes the tie-break draw for every agent and uses it only for the ones on the midpoint, so each agent's tie-break is a function of its position in the iteration rather than of how many agents happened to land on 4.

Phase A for one agent: builds the bank reply prompt, calls gateway.generate, logs the prompt and reply, then checks the reported prompt length against max_prompt_tokens. Returns None on FatalGatewayError, which becomes a logged failure, logging the prompt with an empty response first. No parse-retry loop, unlike the generated regime, because a bank reply is parsed for nothing.

Phase B for one agent: calls gateway.score_next_token, logs the prompt with the raw top logprobs whether or not they score, checks the prompt budget, then scores. Returns None on FatalGatewayError or ProbeMassTooLow, both per-agent events; PromptBudgetExceeded is deliberately not absorbed. Never retried, since the probe is deterministic at temperature 0 and a second call would return the same off-scale answer.

Builds one bank_item row. prompt_token_count, completion_token_count and latency stay summed over the reply and the probe, since every analysis reads them as what the agent-round cost, while the two prompt lengths are also recorded separately because RQ1 reports length per language and a sum of two differently-shaped prompts cannot be split back apart. A row is failed when the probe produced nothing, or when the reply did in any round but round 0, which has no reply by construction; a failed row repeats stance_before as stance_after and leaves every probe column null. A successful row records the probe mean as stance_after and mirrors the reply into both reason_text and reply_text.

This agent's remembered rounds plus the round in progress, appended to a copy so nothing is committed. The probe has to see the reply just written, but a round whose probe then fails must leave no trace. Returns the previous rounds unchanged when the new round has neither reads nor a reply.

Commits one round to an agent's memory, keeping everything when run.memory_rounds is None and the last memory_rounds rounds when a window is configured. Trimmed here as well as in the prompt builder because this dict lives for the whole run. A round with neither reads nor a reply is not remembered, which now means a failed round only, since a delivery: off round reads the neutral message and writes a reply like any other.

Reads interactions.jsonl and returns every row through last_completed_turn, with duplicates resolved. Two interruptions leave two kinds of extra rows: a re-logged round appears twice, resolved by keying on (turn, speaker) and keeping the last write, the same rule export_csv.py applies; a round interrupted part-way appears once and for some agents only, dropped entirely by the turn filter, since counting the half that got written would advance those agents' bank cycles past everyone else's. Returns an empty list when the file does not exist.

Rebuilds the two pieces of bank state that are not in the checkpoint, both from the log and both as of last_completed_turn: each sender's post count per side, skipping round-0 rows that posted nothing, and each agent's remembered rounds, skipping round 0 and any row that failed. Renders remembered posts through _remembered_text in the run's language and applies the memory window only when one is configured. Returns immediately outside the bank regime.

For a GraphSampling strategy, checks every agent id is a node in the graph before anything dispatches. The graph is built from agent_id_for before the population exists, so a mismatch would otherwise surface as every agent raising on turn 1, after the run directory, config and round-0 probe had been written. No-op for alpha sampling.

Checks every agent carries run.language_condition, raising with the offending ids otherwise. True by construction, and checked because live delivery renders a post in its sender's language while the resume path renders remembered posts in the run's language; those agree only while this holds. No-op outside the bank regime.

Writes graph_edges.csv once at run start for a GraphSampling strategy, so analysis has the structure the run actually used rather than one rebuilt from the config under some other networkx version. Idempotent: an existing file is never rewritten, so a resume still gets the file if the first pass died before writing it.

The population in agent-id order. Every per-round draw consumes its stream while iterating this list, so the order is part of what the seed means; sorting explicitly means a future change to how agents are stored cannot silently reorder every draw.

Passes gathered results through, re-raising the first BaseException among them. The two recoverable failures are already absorbed into None by the dispatch helpers, so anything arriving here is an undesigned failure and must surface rather than become a soft-failure row.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::_bui: Returns GraphSampling for neighbor_strategy "graph", built from graph_seed and node ids from agent_id_for because the population does not exist at wiring time, or AlphaSampling(run.alpha, run.N) otherwise.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::_no_: An awaitable returning None, used to hold a position in the Phase B gather for an agent whose reply already failed, so results stay aligned with the agent list.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::_rep: The stripped reply body, or an empty string when there was no reply. Two rows carry an empty reply: the round-0 probe, where none was asked for, and a round whose reply call failed. The log tells them apart, by turn 0 with api_call_status success against failed_logged_null, while the prompt treats them identically because there is nothing to show either way.
functions.tests/conftest.py::bank_gateway: A mock_gateway whose generate returns plain prose instead of a STANCE line, so a bank reply written verbatim into agent memory does not put the word STANCE into later prompts and fail the prompt audit against the fixture rather than the code.
functions.tests/factories.py::make_logprob_respons: Builds a BackendResponse shaped like score_next_token's, with top_logprobs specified three ways in precedence order: raw pairs, a {point: probability} distribution, or mean with all mass on one scale point. off_scale adds probability on a non-digit token for exercising the mass floor. Raises when mean is not a whole scale point, pointing the caller at probabilities instead.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::_bank_run: A minimal bank-regime ExperimentRun over the fixture bank, with a probe question set so the schema accepts it.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::_bank_inter: A successful bank_item Interaction whose stance_after deliberately disagrees with its probe_mean, so a test can tell which column was applied.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::test_bank_r: Applying a bank row records probe_mean as the stance and ignores stance_after, since nothing in a bank reply is parsed for a stance.
The stance record's reason_text comes from reply_text, not from the reason_text column, even when the two differ.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::test_the_ro: A turn-0 row with no reply, no items and no neighbours is applied as the agent's first stance record, so the starting stance is measured in the dataset rather than inferred from initial_stance.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::test_a_bank: Applying a failed bank row raises about the missing probe_mean rather than falling back to stance_after, which would write the agent's previous stance into history as though it had been measured again.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::test_the_ge: A generated-regime row, which has no probe_mean at all, is still applied from stance_after exactly as before.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::test_bank_h: Eight applied bank rows leave eight stance records and a memory_window holding only the last five interaction ids.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::test_bank_s: A probe mean applied before a snapshot is still the agent's current stance after restoring into a fresh manager, which resume depends on.
functions.tests/test_agent_manager.py::test_initia: A generated and a bank run on the same seed produce identical initial stances and personas, so the regime changes only what initial_stance is read for.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::_write_bank: Writes a header plus the given rows to bank.csv under tmp_path and returns the path.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::_row: Builds one CSV row string from item_id, arg_id, strength, side and the four language texts, each defaulted so a test overrides only the field it is exercising.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::_sender_rng: The sender stream exactly as the orchestrator derives it: SeedManager(seed).sender_rng("argument", sender_id).
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_the_fix: The shipped fixture bank loads and reports two pro items and two con items by their sorted ids.
No rendering of any fixture item in any of the four languages contains a digit, so the prompt audit can tell a leaked position number from the argument's own text.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_every_i: Every fixture item has a non-empty rendering in all four languages, and the four are genuinely distinct strings rather than a repeated placeholder.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_both_st: The fixture bank covers both strength labels and both sides, so a test needing either does not have to supply its own bank.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_missing: A nonexistent bank path raises BankValidationError naming the missing file rather than a bare OSError.
A header missing the romanized_hindi and hindi columns raises with both names in the message, so the typo is identifiable from the error alone.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_an_empt: A file with only a header raises about the bank being empty.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_duplica: A repeated item_id raises rather than letting the later row overwrite the earlier one.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_a_missi: A bank with only pro items raises naming the absent con side, since an agent on that side would have nothing to post and there is no safe thing to do at dispatch time.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_empty_t: A blank cell in any of the four language columns, including a whitespace-only one, raises naming that language (5 cases). A blank would otherwise produce an arm in which one argument was silently empty.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_invalid: An unknown side, an unknown or empty strength, an empty arg_id and an empty item_id each raise with a message naming the field (5 cases).
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_every_p: A bank with a bad strength, a blank Hinglish cell, a bad side and consequently no con items reports all four problems in one exception rather than failing on the first.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_errors_: An error message carries both the CSV line number and the item_id, so the offending row is locatable in a large file.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_unknown: An unknown item raises KeyError, an unknown language and an unknown side raise ValueError. Falling back to English would turn one arm of a matched set into a copy of another.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_items_f: Two banks with the same rows in different order report the same sorted side list and make the same pick for the same sender, so re-sorting the CSV cannot change which argument an agent posts.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::_sequence: Posts `rounds` consecutive items for one sender and side, calling record_post after each, and returns the item ids in order.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_no_repe: One full cycle on a side covers every item on that side exactly once.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_the_cyc: Over twelve posts on a four-item side, each block of four is a permutation covering every item once, so the cycle restarts rather than drifting.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_the_two: Posting once on the pro side leaves the sender's next con pick identical to a fresh bank's, so switching sides does not disturb the other side's cycle.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_differe: Four senders working through the same four-item side do not all produce the same order, so two agents on a side are not reciting the bank in unison.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_pick_is: Two picks at the same count return the same item and leave post_counts empty, so a re-derivation after a crash or a second call in one round cannot drift.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_pick_do: The caller's Random has the same state after a pick as before, which is what makes the pick a function of the count rather than of how often it was called.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_the_tur: Picks at turns 1, 2, 5 and 99 for the same count all return one item, so a per-turn derivation is not quietly reshuffling the order each round.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_pick_re: An unknown side and an empty sender_id each raise ValueError rather than being coerced.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_the_sam: The property RQ1's matched sets rest on: the same sender walking the same six-round side sequence picks an identical item list in all four languages, while each item still renders in the language under test. Asserts the consequence rather than the structure, so a language reaching the draw by any route would fail it.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_a_diffe: Seeds 42 and 43 produce different sequences over three full cycles. Compared over twelve posts rather than four because four items admit only 24 orderings, and these two seeds happen to share their first-cycle permutation.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_restore: A bank restored to a count of three makes the same fourth pick as one that posted three times without stopping, which is the resume requirement.
Counts read out with post_counts and put back with restore_post_counts come back unchanged for two senders on different sides.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_post_co: A snapshot taken before a record_post is unaffected by it, so callers cannot mutate the manager's counts through the returned dict.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_restore: Restoring an unknown side or a negative count raises rather than being accepted and silently changing the cycle.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::_bank_confi: Turns the shared valid config dict into a bank-regime one over the fixture bank, with a probe question, then applies any overrides.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_a_vali: A well-formed bank config loads and keeps its regime and bank path.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_a_miss: A nonexistent bank path is reported as a config error quoting the path.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_a_bank: A bank with one empty Hindi cell is rejected at load, naming that cell, so the bank is loaded in full rather than merely stat()ed. Otherwise the run would complete and produce a Hindi arm with one silently blank argument.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_a_one_: A bank with only pro items is rejected at config load, naming the absent con side.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_a_bank: A config with both an out-of-range alpha and a bad side in its bank reports both, so two independent problems take one run to fix.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_bank_r: A bank config with bank_path deleted raises a ConfigLoadError naming the field.
A bank config with probe_question deleted raises, which matters most because an English default would probe every language arm in English.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_the_ge: A generated config with no bank path still loads, so the bank check does not run for runs that do not use one.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_a_grap: A graph-strategy config loads and keeps its strategy and degree.
A degree of 10 at M=8 under the graph strategy is rejected at load with a message about being less than M.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_the_sh: All three shipped RQ1 configs load, use the bank regime and the graph strategy, agree on M, N, K and degree, and carry a probe question and a git commit hash (3 cases). They are the only worked bank examples a researcher has, so one drifting from the schema would be worse than none.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_the_de: A full field-by-field dump of the control and the treatment differ in exactly delivery and run_id, the latter so the two arms do not write into one directory.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_delive: Raw YAML parsing of all three configs gives delivery as a string, since YAML 1.1 reads bare off as False and the schema rejects it. The quotes are load-bearing and a tidy-up would remove them.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::rq1_confi: Fixture returning a writer that copies the shipped RQ1 config, applies the small test run parameters and any overrides, and writes it under tmp_path.
Writes one RQ1 config YAML under tmp_path with the given overrides applied and returns its path.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::_signatur: Everything about a row that must be reproducible across executions: turn, speaker, neighbours, both stances, both text columns, content type, items read and posted, all four probe columns, token counts and status. Excludes interaction_id, timestamp and latency, which are facts about one execution.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_the_: configs/rq1/smoke.yaml loads as a bank, graph, delivery-on run carrying a probe question, a bank path and a commit hash. It is the only worked bank example a researcher has, so drift from the schema would be worse than no example.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_a_fu: A whole run writes 32 rows over turns 0 to 3, 8 final agents each with K+1 stance records, a run_config marked completed with both timestamps, a checkpoint at turn K, and a graph_edges.csv holding 16 edges.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_the_: Read back with pandas, the five stance and probe columns are numeric, content_type is all bank_item, statuses are in the known set, every probe_dist is a 7-element list, and items_read is empty at round 0 and exactly N after.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_expo: A bank run passes through export_csv's load, dedupe and derive steps to 32 rows carrying regime and delivery, with x matching (probe_mean - 4) / 3 and items_read semicolon-joined to N entries.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_a_ma: An English and a Hindi run on one seed produce identical neighbour samples, identical posted items, identical feeds and an identical graph file. The probe is held at a constant reading so the sides match; in a real run divergent readings diverge the sides, which is a result rather than a defect.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_all_: All four language arms produce the same turn, speaker, neighbour, posted-item and items-read signature, including romanized_hindi.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_the_: The English arm's prompts contain the English rendering of a bank item and not the Hindi one, and the Hindi arm's the reverse. The other half of the matched-set claim: a bug rendering every arm in English would pass every structural assertion.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_a_re: A run killed after round 2 of 4 and resumed matches an uninterrupted one on the full row signature, probe distributions and posted items included. Stronger than the generated regime's version because the bank cycle position and the remembered rounds are not in the checkpoint and are rebuilt from the log.
The graph_edges.csv written before a crash is unchanged after the resume, so the file is not rewritten with a possibly different graph.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_the_: A delivery-on and a delivery-off run on one seed produce identical turn, speaker, neighbour and posted-item draws and an identical graph file, so the control's drift is a baseline for the treatment rather than for a different run.
The reproducible draw signature of one run directory: turn, speaker, neighbours and posted item per row, sorted.

Checks every reply and probe prompt of a whole run for three leaks: no prompt mentions STANCE, none shows an agent id or anything calling itself a position, every reply stimulus up to the directive and every probe stimulus up to the question is digit-free, and no probe-specific text appears in any reply prompt. The anchor and instruction lines after the question do name 1 and 7, which the model needs to answer at all.

functions.tests/test_seed_manager.py::test_the_new: All four turn purposes across three turns give twelve distinct first draws, so the argument and probe offsets collide with neither each other nor the original neighbour and meme streams.
functions.tests/test_seed_manager.py::test_graph_s: graph_seed is stable for one base seed, differs across seeds, and collides with none of the three long-lived offsets or the first 49 turns of any purpose offset. functions.tests/test_seed_manager.py::test_sender_: Two managers on the same seed give the same sender the same ten draws, with no turn in the derivation, which is what the bank's no-repeat guarantee depends on.

A purpose that is not a turn purpose, and an empty sender_id, each raise ValueError.
functions.tests/test_seed_manager.py::test_no_cond: Inspects SeedManager.__init__ and asserts its parameters are exactly (self, seed), so there is no language, topic or trial argument for a derivation to mix in. Fails first if someone adds one.

functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::_: An M=8, K=3 bank-regime run over the fixture bank on a degree-4 graph, with a probe question and anchor labels, overridable per test.
Every logged Interaction from a bank run's directory, via the shared reader.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::t: A completed run writes M times (K+1) rows covering turns 0 through K, with exactly M rows per turn.
Reply calls total M times K and probe calls M times (K+1), so a round is two calls per agent plus one probe each at round 0.
Every row is a bank_item with no meme id and all four probe columns populated, and every post-round-0 row carries a posted item, three items read and a reply.

Driving the probe to 4, 6, 2 then 5 across rounds, each row's stance_after is that round's reading and its stance_before is the previous round's, so stance is what the probe measured rather than anything self-reported.
Every turn-0 row has no items read, no posted item, no neighbours and no reply, but does carry a probe mean, so the starting stance is measured rather than inferred.
At K=1 there are 8 reply calls and 16 probes, so round 0 spends probes only.
A run whose first round crashes still has a checkpoint at turn 0 and only turn-0 rows, so a crash in round 1 does not cost the starting measurement and a resume cannot probe round 0 twice.
No reply or probe prompt in a whole run mentions STANCE.
Across every reply and probe prompt of a whole run, none mentions a position or contains an agent id.
With every round-0 reading at 6.0, every round-1 post is a pro item.
With every reading at 2.0, every round-1 post is a con item.

With every reading at exactly 4.0, two runs on the same seed assign identical sides and the population is genuinely split across both sides, so the tie is neither clamped to one side nor left undefined.
The (speaker, side) pairs posted at turn 1 in one run directory, sorted by speaker.
Each row's items_read is exactly what its listed neighbours posted that round, in neighbour order.
Every post-round-0 row lists exactly N neighbours and never the speaker itself.
Every row's neighbours are a subset of that speaker's adjacency in the strategy's own edge list.

graph_edges.csv holds the header and exactly the strategy's edges, M times degree over 2 of them. Analysis needs the structure the run used rather than one rebuilt from the config under a different networkx version.
An alpha-sampling run writes no graph_edges.csv, since there is no graph to record.

A control and a treatment arm on the same seed produce identical turn, speaker, neighbour and posted-item signatures, so every seeded stream consumes identically and the two differ only in what agents saw.
The turn, speaker, neighbours and posted item of every row in one run directory.
Round-1 prompts carry no memory section while round-3 prompts carry one holding two reply lines, so memory accumulates as rounds complete.
Over five rounds with a window of 2, no prompt shows more than two reply lines and at least one shows exactly two.
Every round-1 probe prompt contains the marker text the reply call returned that round, which is why Phase B runs after Phase A. That is the agent's own output, read by nobody else.
No reply prompt in the run contains a probe-only token, the probe's digit instruction or the probe question, so measuring an agent does not change what it is shown next round.
Giving every reply a unique marker, no round's reply markers appear in any prompt of that same round, which is Fix F in the bank regime.

Two runs on one seed with per-call-varying probe readings produce identical posted-item signatures. If items were resolved mid-dispatch, later agents' sides would reflect earlier agents' new readings.
The turn, speaker and posted item of every row in one run directory.

When every reply call fails fatally, each round-1 row is written as failed_logged_null with an empty reply, no probe mean and stance_after equal to stance_before. No invented reply and no stance record.
With every reply failing, only the round-0 probes are spent, since the agent will not be applied this round whatever the probe says.
An off-scale round-1 probe leaves the row failed with null probe columns and an unchanged stance, while the reply text is still present: the reply happened and only the measurement failed.
With round 1's probe failing, each agent's final stance history holds turns 0 and 2 only, and round 2's prompts carry no reply lines, so the failed round spends neither a record nor a memory slot.
A fatal gateway error on every probe leaves all 16 rows written as failed_logged_null rather than aborting the run.
A RuntimeError from a reply call propagates out of the run rather than becoming a soft-failure row, since gather with return_exceptions would otherwise flatten real bugs into return values.
CostCeilingExceeded raised from a probe aborts the whole run rather than being absorbed per agent.
One failed round-0 probe leaves exactly one failed row and round 1 still runs for all 8 agents, that agent falling back to its configured initial_stance for its first side assignment.
A post-round-0 row's prompt tokens, completion tokens and latency are the sums over the reply and the probe, while a round-0 row carries the probe's figures alone.
A bank run is wired with GraphSampling and a BankManager; a default run gets AlphaSampling and no bank.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::m: An autospec'd ModelGateway with a model id and vision support set, for wiring tests that never dispatch.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::t: English and Hindi runs on one seed produce identical edge lists while a different seed does not, so the four arms of a trial share a structure.
Constructing a bank-regime orchestrator with bank=None raises at construction rather than on the first pick, with the run directory and config already written.
The graph's node set equals the initialized population's agent ids, since agent_id_for is shared by the wiring and by initialize_population and a drift would build a graph of non-agents.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::_: Lets the rounds before round_number succeed, then fails every reply. Failing all agents matters: rows are written only after gather returns and _unwrap re-raises first, so the round leaves no partial rows, unlike the known mid-turn re-logging gap.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::t: A run crashing in round 3 leaves turns 0 to 2 logged, and a second pass completes it to turn 4.
After a crash and a resume there are exactly 8 turn-0 rows, one per agent, rather than a doubled starting measurement.
A crashed-and-resumed run and an uninterrupted one post identical items and show identical feeds, which depends on the bank cycle counts being rebuilt from the log rather than restarted.
The turn, speaker, posted item and items read of every row in one run directory.
The rebuilt post counts equal an uninterrupted run's and total M times K. Checked directly because an off-by-one would surface as a subtly different item sequence rather than as an error.

After a crash in round 3, the rebuilt history holds two rounds per agent, each with reads and a reply, and the resumed round-3 prompts carry a memory block with two reply lines. Remembered rounds cannot be checkpointed without putting post text into agent state.
After a five-round run with a window of 2, the rebuilt history holds exactly two rounds per agent.
A round whose probe failed is absent from the rebuilt history, so a resume carries the same memory an uninterrupted run would.
With every logged row duplicated on disk, the rebuilt counts still total M times K rather than twice that, keyed on (turn, speaker) with the last write kept, the same rule export_csv applies.
Re-running a finished run adds no rows and makes no further reply or probe calls.
functions.export_csv.py::_null_out_round_zero_shif: Marks every bank-regime turn-0 row with is_round_zero and nulls stance_before, stance_shift, abs_stance_shift and stance_moved on them. Those rows' stance_after is the probe's starting reading but their stance_before is the configured initial_stance, so a shift there is the gap between a configuration and a measurement, which biased mean_abs_shift, turns_moved and polarization_change upward. Casts stance_moved to the nullable boolean dtype before masking, since masking a numpy bool column would upcast it to object. Generated runs never write turn 0 and return unchanged.
functions.run_simulation.py::_describe_memory: One line saying what an agent carries from round to round: the configured window, or "full history" plus whether a max_prompt_tokens ceiling is set. Spells the default out rather than printing "None rounds", because which of the two a run uses bounds the effect it can measure.
functions.sandbox/interaction_engine.py::GraphSamp: Raises ValueError naming the seed, every node below k and its degree, and the three remedies, when rewiring left any node with fewer than k neighbours. k <= degree is necessary but not sufficient: WS rewiring moves edges instead of adding them, so a node can finish below degree. Raising here rather than in select_neighbors means the run fails before the population, the run directory and the round-0 probe are paid for, and since the graph is a function of the seed alone, all four arms of a matched set fail or none do.
functions.sandbox/logging_writer.py::LoggingWriter: Appends one PromptRecord as a JSON line to prompts.jsonl under the same lock write_interaction uses, rather than a second lock: both files are appended from the same dispatch tasks, the lock is held across one small write, and one lock is one fewer ordering to reason about. Duplicate lines are possible and accepted, since a resumed run re-runs the round its checkpoint does not cover; readers key on (turn, agent_id, call) and keep the last write, as export_csv.py does for interactions.
functions.sandbox/model_gateway.py::ContextLengthE: Raised when the provider reports the prompt did not fit the context window. Deliberately not a FatalGatewayError, so the orchestrator cannot absorb it into one agent's failed row: a prompt overflows because that agent's history grew, so it overflows every round after, and the agents that overflow first are the ones whose language tokenizes least efficiently. Absorbing it would drop one arm's most talkative agents and keep another's, inside the comparison RQ1 reports. It ends the run instead, leaving the choice of a smaller K, a memory window or a longer-context model to the person running it.
functions.sandbox/models.py::PromptRecord: One line of prompts.jsonl: the run, turn, agent and call type, the prompt text verbatim, the response, and for a probe the provider's raw top logprobs before any scoring. Exists because three things cannot be reconstructed from the dataset afterwards: whether a number ever leaked into a prompt, how long each language arm's prompts really were, and what distribution a particular probe_mean came from. response_text is empty on a failed call, since the prompt is still a fact about what was sent.
functions.sandbox/models.py::ExperimentRun.resolve: Replaces a None log_prompts with the regime's default, True for bank and False for generated. Resolved during validation rather than at the point of use so run_config.json records the bool the run acted on; a null there would leave a reader deriving the default from the regime.
functions.sandbox/models.py::ExperimentRun.check_n: For regime="bank" with delivery="off", requires neutral_message to be present and non-blank. Not defaulted, for the reason probe_question is not: a generic fallback would make every arm's control read English. Not merely present either, since a blank message would deliver an empty post to the whole control arm and look in the output like a message that failed to move anyone.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::Prom: Raised when a prompt came back longer than run.max_prompt_tokens. Fatal for the run rather than for one agent, and for ContextLengthExceeded's reason: the agents that overflow first are the ones whose language tokenizes least efficiently, so absorbing it would drop one arm's agents and keep another's. Checked after the call, because the count it compares is the provider's own report of what it received, so the overflowing call is paid for once and then the run stops.

Stores the agent, round, call type, reported token count and ceiling, and builds a message naming all five plus the three remedies (a smaller K, a memory window, a longer-context model). States that nothing was truncated, which is the property the exception exists to preserve.
functions.sandbox/simulation_orchestrator.py::Simu: Returns run.neutral_message, raising ValueError when it is missing or blank. Unreachable through the loader, which already requires it for a delivery-off bank run, and kept for the reason _probe_question's guard is: delivering an empty post to the whole control arm every round would look in the output like a message that moved nobody.

Renders one logged item id back to text on the resume path, reading the reserved neutral id off the run and every other id out of the bank. That split is why a bank may not use the reserved id: two sources for one id would disagree, and only one of them would be what the agent actually read.

Appends one PromptRecord through the logger when run.log_prompts is on, and returns immediately otherwise. Called from inside the dispatch helpers rather than the apply loop, so the record is of the call itself: a call whose round is later discarded still happened and was still paid for, and a prompt audit has to see it. Both regimes honour the flag; only its default differs, and a generated-regime format retry writes a second line for the same key.

Raises PromptBudgetExceeded when the provider's reported prompt_tokens exceeds run.max_prompt_tokens, and returns silently when no ceiling is set. Checks the reported count rather than a local tokenizer estimate, which would be wrong by a different margin in each language arm. Reached from the bank dispatch helpers only: the generated regime's five-turn memory window cannot grow without bound, so there is nothing there to catch.
functions.tests/test_bank_manager.py::test_the_res: A bank whose CSV uses the item id __neutral__ raises BankValidationError with "reserved" in the message. The orchestrator resolves that id from the run rather than the bank, so such a row would never be read and a control row would look like a treatment row that read it.
A bank with both the reserved id and an unknown strength reports both in BankValidationError.errors, so the file takes one run to fix rather than two.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_all_fo: All four shipped RQ1 arm configs load and between them cover english, hinglish, romanized_hindi and hindi with four distinct run ids. The two Roman-script arms are the contrast RQ1 exists to measure, so both ship as worked examples.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_the_rq: Dumps all four arm configs and asserts each differs from the English arm only in run_id, language_condition and probe_question, and that the four probe questions really are distinct. Any other differing field would mean the arms are not one instrument with one factor varied.
functions.tests/test_config_loader.py::test_every_: The four arms' (stance_low_label, stance_high_label) pairs collapse to one, and that pair holds no Devanagari. The labels render inside English sentences, so translating them would code-mix the frame.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_the_: Runs a two-round bank run whose round-0 probes all read 3.0 and whose later probes all read 6.0, exports it, and asserts agents.csv has one row per agent with initial_stance 3.0, final_stance 6.0 and net_drift 3.0. Nulling round 0's stance_before must not empty the column: groupby.first() skips the null and lands on round 1's stance_before, which is the round-0 reading.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_a_ge: A whole generated-regime run exports with is_round_zero false everywhere and no null stance_before or stance_shift, since that regime never writes turn 0.
functions.tests/test_integration_run.py::test_the_: configs/rq1/smoke_off.yaml loads with delivery "off" and a non-blank neutral_message, so the worked example of the E4 control is one the schema accepts.

A whole delivery-off run makes M x K reply calls and M x (K+1) probes, writes 32 rows all carrying a probe mean, and gives every non-zero round items_read of exactly the reserved neutral id plus a non-empty reply. Then checks no bank argument in any language appears in any prompt and the neutral message appears exactly once per reply prompt.

Runs all four arms, strips from each prompt the lines carrying a bank text, an arm's probe question or a language directive, and asserts the remaining skeletons are equal line for line between every arm and English, for replies and probes alike. Also checks the skeleton is neither empty nor the whole prompt, so the filter cannot be making the comparison vacuous, and that the arms do differ where they are allowed to.
Returns True for a prompt line that carries one of the three things allowed to vary: a language directive, one of the four arms' probe questions, or any bank text in any language.
The prompt's lines with every variable line removed, which is the part that must be byte-identical across arms.

Runs each arm, pulls the lean line and the "On this scale" line out of the first probe prompt, and asserts each collapses to a single string across all four arms with no Devanagari in either. The anchor labels sit inside those English sentences, so translating them would code-mix the instrument and change it between arms at once.

Over a three-round run, every one of the M x K reply prompts and M x (K+1) probe prompts has one of the seven rendered lean sentences on the line directly after the topic line. Matched as whole sentences, because the midpoint lean contains the shared fragment twice and a fragment count could not tell one lean from two.
functions.tests/test_interaction_engine.py::test_a: Pins the fact first, that WS(8, 4, 0.1) at seed 30 leaves a node with 2 neighbours, then asserts GraphSampling with k=3 raises at construction with the seed, k, the short degree and the agent id in the message. Caught here rather than on round 1, after the population, the config and the round-0 probe have been paid for.
functions.tests/test_interaction_engine.py::test_t: Seed 45 starves two nodes, and the single error reports "2 node(s)" and both degrees, so a bad graph takes one run to diagnose.
functions.tests/test_interaction_engine.py::test_a: Seed 0 at degree 4 leaves every node at least 3 neighbours, and GraphSampling with k=3 constructs and caches a neighbour list of at least k for every agent.
functions.tests/test_interaction_engine.py::test_t: The seed-30 graph averages above k and still has one node below it, and construction still raises. This is why the schema's k <= graph_degree check is necessary but not sufficient.
functions.tests/test_logging_writer.py::test_concu: Fifty concurrent write_prompt calls produce exactly fifty parseable PromptRecord lines, none torn, with the newline inside a prompt not splitting a line, and no reply line carrying logprobs. prompts.jsonl is appended from the same dispatch tasks as interactions.jsonl and shares its lock.
functions.tests/test_logging_writer.py::test_inter: One interaction and one prompt written through the same writer land one line each in interactions.jsonl and prompts.jsonl, so the shared lock does not mean a shared file.
functions.tests/test_model_gateway.py::test_a_cont: litellm's ContextWindowExceededError raises ContextLengthExceeded from both generate and score_next_token, is not retried, and is not a subclass of FatalGatewayError. The subclass check is the point: the orchestrator absorbs FatalGatewayError per agent, and absorbing an overflow would drop the agents whose language tokenizes least efficiently.
functions.tests/test_models.py::test_the_delivery_: A bank run with delivery="off" and no neutral_message, or a blank one, raises a ValidationError naming the field. A blank message would deliver an empty post to the whole control arm and look like a message that moved nobody.
The same config with a non-empty neutral_message validates and keeps the string verbatim.
functions.tests/test_models.py::test_a_delivery_on: A bank run with delivery left on validates with neutral_message None, so the requirement is conditional on the arm that actually delivers it.
functions.tests/test_models.py::test_the_generated: A generated-regime run with delivery="off" validates with neutral_message None, since delivery is a bank-regime switch the generated loop ignores.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_the_l: At turns 1, 2, 3 and 10 the agent's rendered lean sentence appears exactly once in the bank reply prompt (4 cases). Once, not zero and not twice: it is a permanent trait, and a sentence that vanishes after round 1 makes two consecutive rounds two different instruments.
In every one of those rounds the lean is the line immediately after the topic line (4 cases), so its position in the prompt is fixed rather than drifting with whatever sections happen to be present.

With a full feed and with an empty one, at turns 1, 2 and 5, the lean still appears exactly once (6 cases). The empty-feed case is the one that mattered: with nothing read and nothing in the feed, dropping the lean left every probe after round 0 byte-identical and the control flat by construction.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_full_: With memory_rounds=None and seven remembered rounds, all seven posts appear, there are seven "You replied:" lines, and their positions are in ascending order. Nothing is dropped, because a window bounds the effect the experiment can measure.
A run built without passing memory_rounds has it as None and renders all nine remembered rounds, so full history is the default rather than something a config has to ask for.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_the_p: The probe prompt renders all six remembered rounds, reads included. Both calls of a round must show the same history, or the measurement is of a different agent than the one that replied.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_a_win: memory_rounds=2 against a five-round history renders the last two rounds and none of the first three, so a run that deliberately wants a bounded stimulus can still have one.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_a_rou: A remembered round holding only a reply renders the reply line and no read line. No orchestrator path produces that shape now that the control reads the neutral message, so this pins the builder rather than a live case.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_the_l: The probe prompt carries the lean exactly once with an empty history and with a full one (2 cases). The empty case is the round-0 probe, and withholding the lean afterwards would change the question between the two readings whose difference the experiment reports.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_the_p: In the probe prompt too, the lean is the line immediately after the topic line, matching the reply prompt's layout.
functions.tests/test_prompt_builder.py::test_the_r: For an agent starting at 3, the same rendered lean sentence appears in its round-4 reply prompt and in its probe prompt. The two calls of one round have to describe the agent identically.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_a_gen: A generated run at M=10, K=4 prints exactly one line, "at most 40 LLM calls", with the meme caveat.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_a_ban: A bank run at M=8, K=3 prints 24 reply calls, 32 probe calls and 56 in total, so the round-0 probe is in the budget a researcher reads before starting.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_the_d: The same figures for a delivery-off run, with the neutral message named and the word "none" absent from every line. The control used to make no reply calls, and the printed plan said so.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_the_r: The regime line says "side-free message" for a delivery-off run and "delivery ON" for a treatment one, rather than describing the control as reading nothing.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_descr: describe() prints the neutral message verbatim to stdout, so a reviewer can read the one post the whole control arm is built on, as it already does for the probe question.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_the_m: With memory_rounds unset, the memory line says "full history", never prints "None", and reports that no prompt-length ceiling is set. Which of the two a run uses changes what the experiment can measure, so the default has to read as a decision.
With max_prompt_tokens=4096 the memory line carries that number.
With memory_rounds=2 the line says "last 2 rounds" and does not claim full history.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_only_: A hindi-arm run with a Devanagari probe question and English anchor labels produces no warning, because the labels are English in every arm by design and warning about them would be warning about the design.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_an_en: A hindi-arm run whose probe question is English produces exactly one warning, naming probe_question and not the anchor labels.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_the_r: english, hinglish and romanized_hindi runs never warn (3 cases): nothing short of language identification could tell a Hinglish question from an English one, and a warning nobody believes is one nobody reads.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::_RawBoth: A fake provider response that satisfies both call paths at once: choices[0].message.content for generate and choices[0].logprobs.content[0].top_logprobs for score_next_token, plus a usage block. Lets one patched litellm.acompletion serve a whole run.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::_RawBoth._: Builds the nested SimpleNamespace structure both extractors walk, answering "5" with a single top logprob for that token, and a usage block reporting 10 prompt and 1 completion token.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::_RawBoth.m: Returns a stub dict, since the gateway stores the raw response but nothing in these tests reads it.
functions.tests/test_run_simulation.py::test_launc: Runs launch end to end with probe_top_logprobs=7 and asserts every probe call reaching litellm.acompletion asks for 7 with logprobs true, that there are M x (K+1) of them, and that the reply calls ask for no logprobs. The field was validated and recorded and never passed, so a run asking for 7 asked for 20.

Patches ModelGateway to capture its kwargs and asserts launch passes max_concurrency=3 and top_logprobs=11 from the run. The cap was reachable only from the notebook before, and the bank regime dispatches M calls at once twice per round.
Captures the keyword arguments launch builds the gateway with, then constructs the real one so the run still completes.
With neither field set, launch passes max_concurrency None and top_logprobs 20, the schema default. None is unbounded, which is right for a hosted provider that pools connections itself.
The same capture-then-construct wrapper as the previous test's.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::_: The seven lean sentences rendered against one run's anchor labels, as a set. Whole sentences rather than a shared fragment: the midpoint lean contains "the view that" twice, so counting the fragment cannot tell one lean from two.
The prompt line directly after the topic line, which is where the lean always sits. Lets a test assert the lean's content and its position in one comparison.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::t: A delivery-off run makes M x K generate calls and M x (K+1) probe calls, the same as a treatment arm. It used to make no reply calls, which made the control a different activity rather than the same activity without the manipulated factor.

Every control row succeeds and carries a probe mean; round 0 reads nothing and replies nothing, while every later round reads exactly the reserved neutral id, still records the bank item it would have posted, and has a non-empty reply.
Each control reply prompt carries exactly one "A user posted:" line and it is the neutral message, and no bank argument in the run's language appears in any reply or probe prompt.

Round 1's control prompts carry no memory block, and round 3's carry two remembered reads and two remembered replies. The control's history has to change round over round or the arm cannot show drift even in principle.

No control probe prompt contains a feed heading or a posted line, while at least one carries a memory block. The probe measures and never delivers, in either mode, but its memory grows now that the control has rounds to remember.

All M x (K+1) control probe prompts carry a whole rendered lean sentence on the line after the topic. This arm is where it matters most: nothing else about a delivery-off probe changes between rounds, so a lean shown only at round 0 was the one difference between the starting reading and every later one.

Over a five-round run with memory_rounds None, each agent's round-5 reply and probe prompts carry all four earlier replies in the order they happened, and the probe additionally carries this round's own reply last. Reply texts are zero-padded and terminated so one is never a substring of another.
With memory_rounds=2 over five rounds, each agent's last reply prompt carries rounds 3 and 4 and neither round 1 nor round 2, so a run that asks for a bounded stimulus still gets one.

A reply whose reported prompt length is 900 against max_prompt_tokens=500 raises PromptBudgetExceeded out of the whole run, carrying the call type, the round, both numbers, the agent id and the word "truncated". Nothing is truncated silently, and absorbing this per agent would drop the agents whose language tokenizes least efficiently.
An over-long probe prompt raises too, and surfaces at the round-0 probe, which is the first call of the run.
A run with a generous ceiling completes and writes its full M x (K+1) rows, so setting a ceiling changes nothing else about the run.
With max_prompt_tokens unset, a reply reporting a million prompt tokens is not an error and the run completes.

ContextLengthExceeded raised by the gateway propagates out of run() instead of becoming one agent's failed row, since a per-agent failure would quietly drop the agents with the longest histories and that correlates with the language arm.

With the reply reporting 100 prompt tokens and the probe 70, round-0 rows record (0, 70), later rows record (100, 70), and prompt_token_count equals their sum on every row. RQ1 reports length per language and the two prompts grow for different reasons.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::_: Parses a run's prompts.jsonl into PromptRecord objects, skipping blank lines and preserving file order so a last-write-wins check can be made.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::t: A run writes M x K reply lines and M x (K+1) probe lines to prompts.jsonl, each key unique, every line carrying the run id and non-empty prompt text, with a feed line in every reply and the probe question in every probe, and turn 0 appearing among probes only.

Re-scores each logged probe line's raw logprobs and gets back the probe_mean recorded in that row's interaction, for all twelve probes, after checking the scripted readings really did differ so the comparison cannot pass against a constant.
top_logprobs is None on exactly the reply lines and present on exactly the probe lines, so None means "this was not a probe" rather than "the probe came back empty".
Every reply line's response_text is the text the gateway returned, so the prompt and what it produced are readable together.
When every reply raises FatalGatewayError, all M prompts are still logged with an empty response. A failed call happened and was paid for, and it is the one most worth being able to read.

When round 1's probes answer mostly off-scale, their logged lines still carry the raw logprobs including the off-scale token, while the interaction rows leave probe_mean null. ProbeMassTooLow is diagnosable only from the distribution behind it.
With log_prompts False no prompts.jsonl is created, and the run still writes its full set of interaction rows.
A generated-regime run resolves log_prompts to False and writes no prompts.jsonl, so switching the field on by default would not change what an existing config writes to disk.

A generated run with log_prompts True writes M x K lines, all of call type "reply", all carrying the STANCE contract and none carrying logprobs. The field means the same thing in both regimes; only its default differs.

Two agents and one unparseable first reply produce three logged lines, one of them the unparsable attempt, and keying on (turn, agent, call) with the last write winning leaves two lines, neither of them that attempt. A log showing one line would hide the attempt whose reply could not be parsed.

Crashes after round 3's replies are logged but before its probes finish, resumes, and asserts prompts.jsonl holds duplicate keys, that last-write-wins leaves exactly M x K replies and M x (K+1) probes, and that the surviving round-3 copies are the resumed calls. Documented rather than prevented, since deduplicating would mean reading the file back on every append.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::_: Like _crash_in_round, but every pre-crash reply carries the same text. The row-for-row resume comparisons include reply_text, so holding it constant makes the comparison about the state the resume rebuilt rather than about what the mock happened to say.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::t: Runs five rounds clean, crashes another in round 3, resumes it, and asserts the resumed orchestrator holds five remembered rounds per agent, that round 5's prompts carry four earlier replies, and that the crashed run's rows match the clean run's row for row. Full history makes the rebuild load-bearing in a way a three-round window hid.
One run's rows as comparable tuples: turn, speaker, neighbours, posted item, items read and both stances, sorted by turn and speaker.

The same clean-against-crashed comparison for a delivery-off run over four rounds, including api_call_status. The control has history to rebuild now, and the reserved id in items_read has to render from run.neutral_message rather than through the bank, which would raise a KeyError on it.
The same row tuple as the other resume comparison, with api_call_status added so a silently failed round cannot match a successful one.

After a completed control run, _restore_bank_state rebuilds one history per agent whose every remembered round read exactly the neutral message, resolved from the run rather than looked up in the bank.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::_: Every row's reproducible content, keyed on (turn, speaker) with the last write kept, the rule export_csv.py applies on read. Excludes interaction_id, timestamp and latency, which are facts about one execution rather than properties of the run.
functions.tests/test_simulation_orchestrator.py::t: Stages half of round 3's rows on disk with the checkpoint at round 2, as a crash between two write_interaction calls would leave them, resumes, and asserts the deduplicated rows match an uninterrupted run's exactly. Counting those rows put the written agents' bank cycles a step ahead of everyone else's, so whether a resumed run posted the right arguments depended on where the crash landed.

With checkpoint_every_n_turns=2, round 3 completes and round 4 dies, leaving the whole of round 3 logged and uncheckpointed. The resumed run's deduplicated rows still match an uninterrupted run's, so a full uncommitted round is ignored too, not only a partial one.

Asserts the mechanism directly: against a three-round log, _restore_bank_state(1) rebuilds one round of post counts and one remembered round per agent, and _rebuild_last_posts(1) returns only turn-1 posts.
