groups.summary: Population creation, persona cycling past the pool size, seeded stance reproducibility, the memory_window cap, and snapshot/restore isolation.

tests.summary: With M larger than the pool, personas repeat in order, so each persona is shared by several agents rather than running out.
Two managers with identically seeded RNGs draw the same initial stances in the same order.
An unknown agent id raises KeyError uncaught, since it is a programmer error rather than a data case.
A vanished persona pool raises at initialize time, so the manager does not trust the config loader's earlier check.
Applying interactions appends stance history and keeps memory_window to the agent's own most recent 5 interaction ids.
Mutating the manager after a snapshot leaves the snapshot unchanged, which is what the deep copy guarantees.
Restoring reproduces every agent exactly, and the restored manager is isolated from the passed-in list.
Applying a bank row records probe_mean as the stance and ignores stance_after, since nothing in a bank reply is parsed for a stance.
The stance record's reason_text comes from reply_text, not from the reason_text column, even when the two differ.
A turn-0 row with no reply, no items and no neighbours is applied as the agent's first stance record, so the starting stance is measured in the dataset rather than inferred from initial_stance.

Applying a failed bank row raises about the missing probe_mean rather than falling back to stance_after, which would write the agent's previous stance into history as though it had been measured again.
A generated-regime row, which has no probe_mean at all, is still applied from stance_after exactly as before.
Eight applied bank rows leave eight stance records and a memory_window holding only the last five interaction ids.
A probe mean applied before a snapshot is still the agent's current stance after restoring into a fresh manager, which resume depends on.
A generated and a bank run on the same seed produce identical initial stances and personas, so the regime changes only what initial_stance is read for.

groups.summary: Bank loading and validation, the no-repeat pick cycle, and the matched-set property: that every problem in a bad CSV is reported at once with its line, and that a pick is idempotent, turn-independent, language-independent and restorable from counts alone.

tests.summary: The shipped fixture bank loads and reports two pro items and two con items by their sorted ids.
No rendering of any fixture item in any of the four languages contains a digit, so the prompt audit can tell a leaked position number from the argument's own text.
Every fixture item has a non-empty rendering in all four languages, and the four are genuinely distinct strings rather than a repeated placeholder.
The fixture bank covers both strength labels and both sides, so a test needing either does not have to supply its own bank.
A nonexistent bank path raises BankValidationError naming the missing file rather than a bare OSError.
A header missing the romanized_hindi and hindi columns raises with both names in the message, so the typo is identifiable from the error alone.
A file with only a header raises about the bank being empty.
A repeated item_id raises rather than letting the later row overwrite the earlier one.
A bank with only pro items raises naming the absent con side, since an agent on that side would have nothing to post and there is no safe thing to do at dispatch time.

A blank cell in any of the four language columns, including a whitespace-only one, raises naming that language (5 cases). A blank would otherwise produce an arm in which one argument was silently empty.
An unknown side, an unknown or empty strength, an empty arg_id and an empty item_id each raise with a message naming the field (5 cases).
A bank with a bad strength, a blank Hinglish cell, a bad side and consequently no con items reports all four problems in one exception rather than failing on the first.
An error message carries both the CSV line number and the item_id, so the offending row is locatable in a large file.
An unknown item raises KeyError, an unknown language and an unknown side raise ValueError. Falling back to English would turn one arm of a matched set into a copy of another.
Two banks with the same rows in different order report the same sorted side list and make the same pick for the same sender, so re-sorting the CSV cannot change which argument an agent posts.
One full cycle on a side covers every item on that side exactly once.
Over twelve posts on a four-item side, each block of four is a permutation covering every item once, so the cycle restarts rather than drifting.
Posting once on the pro side leaves the sender's next con pick identical to a fresh bank's, so switching sides does not disturb the other side's cycle.
Four senders working through the same four-item side do not all produce the same order, so two agents on a side are not reciting the bank in unison.
Two picks at the same count return the same item and leave post_counts empty, so a re-derivation after a crash or a second call in one round cannot drift.
The caller's Random has the same state after a pick as before, which is what makes the pick a function of the count rather than of how often it was called.
Picks at turns 1, 2, 5 and 99 for the same count all return one item, so a per-turn derivation is not quietly reshuffling the order each round.
An unknown side and an empty sender_id each raise ValueError rather than being coerced.

The property RQ1's matched sets rest on: the same sender walking the same six-round side sequence picks an identical item list in all four languages, while each item still renders in the language under test. Asserts the consequence rather than the structure, so a language reaching the draw by any route would fail it.

Seeds 42 and 43 produce different sequences over three full cycles. Compared over twelve posts rather than four because four items admit only 24 orderings, and these two seeds happen to share their first-cycle permutation.
A bank restored to a count of three makes the same fourth pick as one that posted three times without stopping, which is the resume requirement.
Counts read out with post_counts and put back with restore_post_counts come back unchanged for two senders on different sides.
A snapshot taken before a record_post is unaffected by it, so callers cannot mutate the manager's counts through the returned dict.
Restoring an unknown side or a negative count raises rather than being accepted and silently changing the cycle.
A bank using the reserved id __neutral__ is rejected with "reserved" in the message.
The reserved id is accumulated with the other row errors, not raised alone.

groups.summary: Save and load round-tripping, that a second save leaves only the latest, that a corrupt checkpoint raises, and that no .tmp file survives a successful write.

tests.summary: No checkpoint returns None, which is how a fresh run is detected.
A saved checkpoint reloads with its run id, turn and full agent state intact.
A second save replaces the first, since only the latest resume point is ever needed.
A corrupt checkpoint raises rather than silently restarting at turn 0 and discarding completed work.
save creates its own checkpoints directory, unlike the logging writer.
The temporary file is gone after a successful save, confirming the write-then-rename completed.
The checkpoint on disk is valid JSON, so the atomic rename did not leave it torn.

groups.summary: Every config rejection path, including that two independent errors both surface in one ConfigLoadError, that YAML-supplied git_commit_hash is ignored, and that unknown keys are named.

tests.summary: A valid config loads into an ExperimentRun with git_commit_hash resolved from the working tree.
A hash written into the YAML is discarded and replaced by the real HEAD, so a config cannot claim a commit it did not run against.
A nonexistent config path raises ConfigLoadError rather than an OSError.
Unparseable YAML surfaces as ConfigLoadError, keeping the documented contract that every failure is one error type.
A missing required field is named in the error message rather than reported generically.
N greater than or equal to M is rejected at load time.
Memes enabled with no pool id fails on the schema validator, before any filesystem lookup is attempted.
A meme pool id that resolves to no file is rejected, and the error names the path it looked for.
A meme-enabled config pointing at the real fixture pool loads cleanly.
A config with a bad field and a missing asset reports both in one ConfigLoadError. This is why errors accumulate instead of failing fast, a deliberate deviation from the design doc's sample.
A missing persona pool is reported on its own, so the asset check does not depend on schema validation having failed.
Any mode but multi_turn is rejected, since there is exactly one simulation mode.
YAML that parses to a list, string or number is rejected as ConfigLoadError rather than crashing on the dict operations that follow.
The error names the config the caller passed, not the placeholder path the git-hash helper raises with.
The missing-file error names the real path too.
Errors render as 'field: message' rather than raw Pydantic dicts, which repeated the whole input payload once per error.
An unknown key is reported by name with a typo hint, rather than as the bare extra_forbidden type.
A well-formed bank config loads and keeps its regime and bank path.
A nonexistent bank path is reported as a config error quoting the path.

A bank with one empty Hindi cell is rejected at load, naming that cell, so the bank is loaded in full rather than merely stat()ed. Otherwise the run would complete and produce a Hindi arm with one silently blank argument.
A bank with only pro items is rejected at config load, naming the absent con side.
A config with both an out-of-range alpha and a bad side in its bank reports both, so two independent problems take one run to fix.
A bank config with bank_path deleted raises a ConfigLoadError naming the field.
A bank config with probe_question deleted raises, which matters most because an English default would probe every language arm in English.
A generated config with no bank path still loads, so the bank check does not run for runs that do not use one.
A graph-strategy config loads and keeps its strategy and degree.
A degree of 10 at M=8 under the graph strategy is rejected at load with a message about being less than M.

All three shipped RQ1 configs load, use the bank regime and the graph strategy, agree on M, N, K and degree, and carry a probe question and a git commit hash (3 cases). They are the only worked bank examples a researcher has, so one drifting from the schema would be worse than none.
A full field-by-field dump of the control and the treatment differ in exactly delivery and run_id, the latter so the two arms do not write into one directory.
Raw YAML parsing of all three configs gives delivery as a string, since YAML 1.1 reads bare off as False and the schema rejects it. The quotes are load-bearing and a tidy-up would remove them.
All four shipped arm configs load and cover the four language conditions with distinct run ids.
The four arms differ only in run_id, language_condition and probe_question, and their questions are all different.
All four arms carry one identical pair of anchor labels, with no Devanagari in it.

groups.summary: Cost arithmetic and accumulation, that an unpriced combination raises instead of charging zero, ceiling behaviour, and that concurrent record() calls lose no updates.

tests.summary: Cost is computed from the per-1k rates and accumulates across calls.
An unpriced provider, model or modality raises ValueError rather than charging zero and understating the run's cost.
The breaching call is counted before CostCeilingExceeded is raised, so the reported total includes it.
With no ceiling configured, no total ever raises.
Text and vision calls are priced from their own rate entries.
Many threads recording at once produce the exact expected total, so no update is lost.
A missing pricing table raises FileNotFoundError when the tracker is built, before any call is made.

groups.summary: The builders themselves: that their defaults validate, that overrides still go through validation, and that the mock gateway both returns a parseable reply and rejects calls breaking the real signature.

tests.summary: The run builder's defaults validate and individual fields can be overridden.
An invalid override still raises, so the builder cannot be used to construct an impossible run.
make_agent accepts id and stance positionally, the shape the interaction-engine tests rely on.
The default interaction is a valid generated-text row.
Passing content_type and meme_id together builds a valid meme row.
A meme row with no meme_id is rejected by the model's own validator, not papered over by the builder.
A failed_logged_null row can be built, and reports itself as invalid for analysis.
The builder's reply text parses through the real parser, so mocked replies match what production accepts.
The default backend response body parses.
A text override produces a body the parser rejects, which is how the retry path is driven.
The mock gateway fixture returns something the orchestrator can actually consume.
The mock rejects a call that would not match the real signature. This pins the autospec behaviour, since replacing generate with a bare AsyncMock still works but silently stops catching drift.
The text-only fixture reports supports_vision False, so the fallback path is actually exercised.

groups.summary: End to end, YAML on disk to interactions.jsonl: the shipped example config loads, a full run writes correct output, the same seed reproduces a run exactly, a resumed run matches an uninterrupted one, and agent state agrees with the log.

tests.summary: configs/example_run.yaml loads through the real loader, so the documented example cannot rot unnoticed.
The example config's commented-out meme block validates when enabled, so the documented snippet actually works.
The whole path from a YAML file to all four output files, with only the LLM call faked. The first test to exercise more than one production module together.
A meme-enabled run produces rows whose content_type, meme_id and stance all come from the dataset.
Re-running a finished config writes nothing further, the resume behaviour the launcher documents.
Two runs on one seed produce byte-identical logs on the fields that matter, the end-to-end reproducibility claim.
Each agent's final stance_history matches the rows logged for it, so the two outputs cannot disagree.
A run interrupted and resumed produces the same output as one that never stopped, which is what the per-turn derived streams and the rebuilt last-posts map exist to guarantee.
Every column the planned analysis tier needs is present and populated on each row, checked before that tier exists.
prompt_token_count is populated on text rows, the column that makes the per-language prompt-length gap measurable at all.

configs/rq1/smoke.yaml loads as a bank, graph, delivery-on run carrying a probe question, a bank path and a commit hash. It is the only worked bank example a researcher has, so drift from the schema would be worse than no example.

A whole run writes 32 rows over turns 0 to 3, 8 final agents each with K+1 stance records, a run_config marked completed with both timestamps, a checkpoint at turn K, and a graph_edges.csv holding 16 edges.

Read back with pandas, the five stance and probe columns are numeric, content_type is all bank_item, statuses are in the known set, every probe_dist is a 7-element list, and items_read is empty at round 0 and exactly N after.
A bank run passes through export_csv's load, dedupe and derive steps to 32 rows carrying regime and delivery, with x matching (probe_mean - 4) / 3 and items_read semicolon-joined to N entries.

An English and a Hindi run on one seed produce identical neighbour samples, identical posted items, identical feeds and an identical graph file. The probe is held at a constant reading so the sides match; in a real run divergent readings diverge the sides, which is a result rather than a defect.
All four language arms produce the same turn, speaker, neighbour, posted-item and items-read signature, including romanized_hindi.

The English arm's prompts contain the English rendering of a bank item and not the Hindi one, and the Hindi arm's the reverse. The other half of the matched-set claim: a bug rendering every arm in English would pass every structural assertion.

A run killed after round 2 of 4 and resumed matches an uninterrupted one on the full row signature, probe distributions and posted items included. Stronger than the generated regime's version because the bank cycle position and the remembered rounds are not in the checkpoint and are rebuilt from the log.
The graph_edges.csv written before a crash is unchanged after the resume, so the file is not rewritten with a possibly different graph.

A delivery-on and a delivery-off run on one seed produce identical turn, speaker, neighbour and posted-item draws and an identical graph file, so the control's drift is a baseline for the treatment rather than for a different run.

Checks every reply and probe prompt of a whole run for three leaks: no prompt mentions STANCE, none shows an agent id or anything calling itself a position, every reply stimulus up to the directive and every probe stimulus up to the question is digit-free, and no probe-specific text appears in any reply prompt. The anchor and instruction lines after the question do name 1 and 7, which the model needs to answer at all.
agents.csv keeps initial_stance, and it is now the round-0 probe reading rather than the configured value.
A generated run exports with no round-zero rows and no nulled shifts.
The shipped control config loads with delivery off and a real neutral message.
The control makes a treatment arm's calls, reads only the reserved neutral id, and sees no bank argument.
Whole runs of all four arms produce prompts identical line for line outside the bank text, the question and the directive.
The lean line and the scale line are one English string across all four arms.
Every reply and probe prompt of a three-round run carries a whole lean sentence after the topic line.

groups.summary: Alpha extremes (homophilous at 1, roughly uniform at 0), the N-distinct-never-self contract, seeded reproducibility, and that zero, negative, NaN and mismatched sampling weights all raise.

tests.summary: An alpha below 0 or above 1 raises at construction rather than being clamped into range.
An N below 1 raises at construction.
At alpha 1 the selected neighbours are the closest-stance candidates, the maximally homophilous end of the mechanism.
At alpha 0, selection frequency across many seeds is roughly uniform, the no-echo-chamber end.
Every draw returns exactly N distinct agents and never the speaker, the contract the protocol states.
Fewer than N candidates raises ValueError rather than returning a short list.
Identically seeded streams produce identical neighbour sets.
At turn 1 the engine reads initial_stance even for an agent that somehow has history, which is what keeps the frozen-snapshot reading well defined.
A zero weight raises, since the sampling key formula divides by it.
A negative weight raises. It is worse than an error: it would sort first and be guaranteed selected, a silent wrong answer in the module whose contract is to never clamp.
A NaN weight raises, since it would make the sort order meaningless.
Mismatched weight and item counts raise rather than silently truncating.
For every agent, the chosen set is a subset of its graph adjacency, excludes the speaker itself, and holds exactly k distinct agents.
The same speaker draws the same neighbours from a population with varied stances and from one where every stance is identical, so the selection effect the graph exists to remove is actually gone.
Two strategies on the same graph seed have identical edge lists and draw the same neighbours for every speaker under the same rng, which two arms of a matched set depend on.
Graph seeds 42 and 43 produce different edge lists.

k above degree is rejected at construction, and a node whose cached neighbourhood is smaller than k raises at call time naming how many were needed. A short feed is a different stimulus and would be a confound nothing in the output records.
A speaker that is not a graph node raises rather than being sampled from an empty candidate set, since the graph is built once from the initial population.

An odd degree, a degree below 2, a degree at or above the population, an out-of-range rewire probability, a k below 1 and a k above degree each raise with a matching message rather than being clamped.
A repeated agent id raises, since node indices map to ids positionally and a duplicate would make two nodes the same agent and silently halve the population.
The edge list is sorted, every pair is ordered, the count is exactly M times degree over 2 since rewiring moves edges rather than adding or dropping them, and every agent appears.

Rebuilding a networkx graph from the reported edges at a high rewire probability is connected, confirming the connected WS variant is in use. A disconnected population would be two smaller experiments sharing an output file.

The chosen set matches one reference rng.sample over the sorted candidates, and both streams are at the same position afterwards. Checked by stream state because one call's output alone cannot distinguish sampling once from sampling twice and returning the second.
Turns 1 and 9 under the same rng give the same neighbours, so the turn argument is genuinely unused and the per-round variation comes from the stream the orchestrator derives.
A seed whose rewiring starves one node raises at construction, naming the seed, k, the degree and the agent.
Two starved nodes are both reported in one error.
A seed with no short node constructs and caches at least k neighbours per agent.
A graph averaging above k is still rejected when one node is below it.

groups.summary: That concurrent appends to both jsonl files produce N untorn parseable lines, that the two files stay separate, that both one-shot writes round-trip through their models, that agents_final overwrites, and that a missing run_dir raises.

tests.summary: Many concurrent appends produce exactly N parseable lines with none torn, which is what the lock is for.
run_config.json reloads into an equivalent ExperimentRun.
agents_final.jsonl holds one parseable Agent line per agent.
A second call leaves only the second list, confirming overwrite rather than append.
Writing into a directory that does not exist raises, since creating the run directory is the orchestrator's job.
Fifty concurrent prompt appends give fifty parseable lines, newlines inside prompts included.
One shared lock, two files: an interaction and a prompt land one line each.

groups.summary: Injection decisioning across disabled, rate 0, rate 1 and fixed-turn schedules, seeded reproducibility, the empty and missing pool error paths, and that every image path in the real pool resolves on disk.

tests.summary: With injection disabled every speaker gets None even at rate 1.0, and no pool is loaded at all.
Rate 0 injects nothing across many turns.
Rate 1 under the random schedule injects for every speaker on every turn.
Under fixed_turn, injection happens only on the configured turns and nowhere else.
Two managers with identically seeded streams make the same per-agent injection decisions.
A pool file that parses to no records raises ValueError at construction rather than yielding an unsamplable empty pool.
A missing pool file raises FileNotFoundError at construction.
Every image path in the shipped fixture pool exists on disk. A pre-flight audit found two missing, which would have raised for roughly two sampled memes in three.

groups.summary: Retry versus fatal classification, construction-time vision resolution, cost recording with the bare model id and correct modality, that latency is measured rather than read off the response, api_base forwarding, and that the concurrency cap holds including across retries.

tests.summary: A transient error followed by a success retries and returns the successful response.
An authentication error raises FatalGatewayError immediately, with exactly one provider call.
An unknown model id raises at construction rather than defaulting to text-only and silently misclassifying a vision model.
A call with no image records cost under the text modality.
A call with image bytes records cost under the vision modality.
release is called exactly once after a successful call.
release still runs exactly once when the provider call raises, since it sits in a finally block.
Cost is recorded under the bare model id, not the prefixed one. Passing the prefixed form looked up a doubly-qualified key and failed for every model but a bare OpenAI one.
Every model in the pricing table prices successfully through a real tracker.
Latency comes from the gateway's own clock, matching the elapsed time rather than any provider field.

A response lacking the field the design doc's sample reads still works. Reading it raised AttributeError, which neither error class covers, so it would have aborted the whole run on the first successful call.
Every self-hosted, Ollama and free-tier model id in the vision tables constructs without raising.
A configured api_base reaches the litellm call, which is the only way a local server is reachable at all.
With no api_base configured, None is forwarded, leaving hosted-provider routing unchanged.
Every model id the vision tables recognize that is meant to be runnable has a pricing entry, so a run cannot die at record() time.
With a cap configured, in-flight requests never exceed it. Without the cap a turn opens M connections and the surplus accumulates until the server starts closing them.
With no cap, concurrency rises above any single-digit bound, preserving the previous behaviour for hosted providers.
Capping delays requests without dropping any: every call still completes.
A retrying call holds its slot rather than taking a second one, so retries cannot push past the cap.
A probe call returns the token and logprob pairs in order, the sampled token as text, both token counts, and a non-negative integer latency.

The pairs the gateway produces are fed to probe_scorer.score and give a mean between 5 and 6, closing the loop between the two modules. Asserting the parse alone would not catch a drift in the shape they agree on.

The probe call passes max_tokens 1, temperature 0.0, logprobs True and the configured top_logprobs count. Sampling temperature would add noise to the thing being measured and a second token would be read by nothing.
Gateways constructed at 1, 5, 20 and 50 each forward that count, so the value lives on the run and is recorded rather than hard-coded. A run probed at 5 is not comparable to one probed at 20.
A top_logprobs of 0 raises when the gateway is built, rather than at the first probe.
The probe forwards api_base, so it reaches the same self-hosted server the replies do rather than a hosted provider.

A probe records one cost entry with the text modality and both token counts. The bank regime makes two calls per agent per round, so a probe path recording nothing would under-report a run's cost by about half.
The rate limiter is released once after a successful probe and again after one that raises a fatal error, so a failing probe cannot leak a lease.
A rate-limit error followed by a good response results in two calls and a successful probe, so the retry policy covers the probe path.
An authentication error raises FatalGatewayError after exactly one call.

A BadRequestError about logprobs raises FatalGatewayError after one call, since retrying cannot make a server grow the feature and the run should stop rather than burn three attempts per agent per round.

Absent logprobs, empty or None content, empty top_logprobs and no choices each raise FatalGatewayError naming that level and mentioning logprobs (5 cases). An empty list would instead fail in the scorer once per agent per round, which reads like a model refusing to answer.
A top_logprobs entry with a None logprob raises FatalGatewayError naming the missing field rather than being skipped.
Logprobs arriving as plain dicts, as some providers produce after litellm round-trips them through JSON, parse to the same pairs as the attribute-style shape.
generate passes neither logprobs nor max_tokens and returns top_logprobs None, so None on a reply means this was not a probe rather than a probe that came back empty.

Forty probes against a cap of 4 peak at exactly 4. A probe path outside the semaphore would double the in-flight count the cap bounds, and the failure mode looks like a healthy server dropping the run.
Ten replies and ten probes dispatched together peak at the cap of 3 across both kinds, since the server's batch size bounds total requests rather than requests per kind.
All forty probes behind a cap of 4 complete and every one carries logprobs, so the semaphore bounds concurrency without dropping work.
An overflow raises ContextLengthExceeded from both calls, is not retried, and is not a FatalGatewayError.

groups.summary: Schema-level guarantees: the memory_window cap on construction and on assignment, that in-place append bypasses it, extra=forbid on both config models, and that a stance_scale of two identical values is rejected.

tests.summary: A memory_window of 6 entries is rejected at construction by the field's own length cap.
Assigning an over-cap memory_window raises, which is what validate_assignment exists for: without it the cap would hold only by convention in calling code.
Assigning exactly 5 entries is accepted, so the cap is inclusive.
Documents the known limit: appending in place grows the list past 5 because Pydantic cannot observe mutation. This is why the prompt builder re-slices at the point of use.
validate_assignment applies to every field, not just memory_window: an empty persona is rejected on assignment too.
current_stance returns initial_stance with no history, and the last recorded value once there is one.
An unrecognized top-level config key raises rather than being silently absorbed into a default.
An unrecognized key inside the meme block raises too, the case that would otherwise turn RQ3's meme arm into a second control arm.
Forbidding extras does not break the legitimate optional fields, which still load.
A scale of two identical values is rejected, since min equals max would make every reply but one unparseable.
Two distinct values satisfy the validator, so the check counts distinct values rather than demanding more entries.

Each of the four conditions is accepted on both ExperimentRun and Agent (4 cases). romanized_hindi is distinct from hinglish because Hindi in Roman script is not Hindi-English code-mixing, and RQ1 manipulates language and script separately.
The British spelling "romanised_hindi" is rejected on both Agent and ExperimentRun, so the two cannot drift and leave an agent carrying a condition its own run rejects.

Every new field defaults to the pre-bank behaviour: alpha sampling, generated regime, delivery on, no bank path or probe question, degree 6 at p 0.1, 20 top logprobs, a 0.5 mass floor and a 3-round memory.
An unknown regime or delivery, a rewire probability outside [0,1], a zero top-logprobs count, a mass floor at or below 0 or above 1, a zero memory window and a zero degree each raise (9 cases).
A floor of exactly 1.0 is accepted, since the interval is (0, 1] and "every digit or nothing" is strict but legitimate.
An odd degree raises even when the graph is unused, because it is not representable in a Watts-Strogatz ring at all.
The default degree of 6 is accepted at M=5 under alpha sampling but rejected once neighbor_strategy is graph, so existing small-population configs are not rejected over a field they never read.
N above graph_degree raises at config load rather than per agent on turn 1, since every node starts with exactly degree neighbours and rewiring only removes some.
M=8, N=3 and degree 4 under the graph strategy loads and keeps both values.

regime=bank with either field absent, or blank, raises naming the missing one (5 cases). A missing probe_question is the dangerous case, since an English default would probe every language arm in English.
A bank run carrying both a bank path and a probe question validates and keeps the path.
A generated run with no bank path still loads, so the requirement is genuinely conditional on the regime.
A mistyped probe_mass_flor raises rather than loading at the 0.5 default, so extra=forbid still covers the new field block.
A bank_item row with no bank fields set defaults items_read to empty, posted_item_id and all four probe columns to None, and reply_text to an empty string.
A bank_item row carrying a meme_id raises, keeping the RQ3 meme mechanism and the RQ1 bank mechanism distinguishable in the column every analysis filters on.
Both Interaction and StanceRecord accept turn 0, which the round-0 probe needs.
Relaxing the turn bound to 0 did not open it to negatives.
A turn-0 bank row with an empty neighbour list validates, since nobody has been sampled yet at round 0.
A generated_text or meme row with an empty neighbour list raises (2 cases), preserving what the original min_length=1 caught: sampling that silently produced nothing.
A fully populated bank row keeps its items, posted item and probe fields, and its probe_dist survives a JSON dump and reparse.
A probe_dist of length 0, 6 or 8 raises (3 cases), since a different support would mean probe_mean is not the mean of that distribution.
A delivery-off bank run with a missing or blank neutral_message fails validation.
The same config with a real message validates and keeps it verbatim.
The requirement is conditional: a treatment arm validates without one.
A generated run ignores delivery, so delivery="off" there needs no message.

groups.summary: The probe arithmetic, hand-computed rather than recorded: whitespace and duplicate digit tokens, off-scale tokens that cost mass without contributing, the mass floor as a refusal rather than a clamp, and the distributions that share a mean and differ in side_conf.

tests.summary: A read of 5 at 0.5, 6 at 0.3, 2 at 0.1 and prose at 0.1 gives mass 0.9, mean exactly 5.0, side_conf 0.8/0.9 and a dist summing to 1, all worked out by hand rather than recorded from the code.
dist has one entry per scale point and sums to 1, and equal mass on 1 and 7 gives a mean of exactly 4.
For each of the seven points, all probability on that digit reads back as that mean with mass 1.0.
A " 3" token scores as 3. Without this, providers that prefix whitespace would appear to put no mass on the scale and every probe would fail the floor.
"3" and " 3" in the same response are summed into one answer rather than counted as two points.
Newline, trailing-space, both-sides and tab variants of a digit token all read as that digit (4 cases).
A "0", an "8", a multi-digit number, a word, an empty or blank token, a decimal and a negative all add nothing to the mean while still counting against the mass (10 cases).
A read with 0.2 on the scale and the rest on a refusal raises ProbeMassTooLow carrying both the observed mass and the floor, instead of renormalizing the remainder into a confident stance.
A response entirely on prose raises ProbeMassTooLow with mass exactly 0.0.
Mass equal to the floor counts as a read, since the comparison is strict. Guards against an off-by-one that would reject half the probes in a run whose floor sits at the typical mass.
The same 0.7-on-scale read passes a 0.5 floor and raises against a 0.9 floor, so the floor is doing the work rather than a fixed threshold.
A floor of 0.0, a negative, or one above 1 raises ValueError naming mass_floor (3 cases).
An empty input raises ValueError about nothing to score rather than ProbeMassTooLow, keeping a wiring problem distinct from a model answering off-scale.
With the mean exactly at the midpoint, side_conf becomes P(s = 4) rather than a tail, since there is no side to be confident about.
All mass on 4 and mass split evenly between 1 and 7 share a mean of 4 but give side_conf 1.0 and 0.0, which is the case the column exists for.
A mean of 3.2 reports P(s < 4) and a mean of 4.8 reports P(s > 4), both 0.7 for the mirrored distributions.
Mass on 4 belongs to neither tail, so a read of 0.8 on 4 and 0.2 on 5 gives side_conf 0.2 rather than near-certainty.
Assigning to a returned ProbeScore's mean raises, so nothing downstream can edit a measurement in place and have the edit reach the log.
Reads of 0.95 and 0.51 on the digit 5 both give mean 5.0 but report their own raw mass, which is the only thing separating a trustworthy read from a marginal one.

groups.summary: That the three language conditions differ only in the directive line and stay within a bounded length spread, the Fix A five-turn memory slice, turn-1 neighbour omission, the one-image meme rule and its downgrade flag, and that a retry changes only the format block.

tests.summary: English, Hinglish and Hindi all produce a prompt containing their own directive.
Prompts for two conditions are identical except the directive line, which is what keeps RQ1's comparison unconfounded by prompt shape.
The three directives stay within a bounded length of each other, so no condition carries a systematically longer instruction.
On a full prompt with memory and neighbours the between-condition length difference is negligible, bounding the confound at the point the model sees it.
An unknown condition raises rather than quietly rendering as English, which would make a misconfigured run look valid.
A reply following the prompt's own format parses cleanly through the real parser, so the two contracts actually agree.
The format block tells the model to put the number on the STANCE line only, because the parser strips every occurrence from the reason text.
The rendered bounds come from the configured scale rather than being hardcoded.
Both anchor labels appear, so a bare number means the same thing to every agent on every turn.
With more than five history entries only the last five render.
The slice still holds when history was grown by in-place append, which the schema cannot catch. This is the cap that actually reaches the model.
A short history renders all of it, not a padded five.
With no history the memory section is absent rather than an empty heading.
Turn 1 has no neighbour block, since bare initial stances with no reasoning would be a stimulus with no analogue later.
Later turns render each neighbour's id, position and reasoning.
A meme neighbour on a vision backend yields image bytes alongside the text.
On a text-only backend the meme becomes caption text with no image, and the fallback flag is set.
The text-only path builds successfully for a meme whose image is absent, proving no disk read happens.
With two meme neighbours exactly one image is attached and the flag records that the other degraded, since the gateway takes only one image.
An all-text neighbour set yields no image and no fallback flag.
The rendered meme framing matches what vision_fallback produces, so the wording is not duplicated here and cannot drift.
A neighbour post naming an unknown meme id raises, surfacing a disagreement between the log and the pool.
A retry changes only the format block. Altering persona, topic, memory or neighbours would mean the logged row answers a different stimulus than a first attempt, mixing two conditions in one dataset.
The emphasised block still describes a format the real parser accepts.
Building leaves the agent and neighbour posts untouched, which matters because the caller passes the frozen snapshot.
A whole-number stance renders as an integer while a fractional one keeps its decimal.
All four language conditions have a directive and no two directives are the same string.
The romanized_hindi directive names Roman script, rules out Devanagari explicitly, and does not mention Hinglish, so it is distinguishable from both neighbouring arms.
Each of the four conditions produces a bank prompt carrying its own directive.

No digit appears anywhere before the language directive, at turns 1, 2 and 5 (3 cases). This is the reason the probe exists: an agent that can see a position number can move its own number towards the ones it was shown, and the result would look exactly like persuasion.
No agent id appears in a bank reply prompt. An id is a stable handle an agent could track across rounds, which turns a feed of arguments into a feed of sources.
Neither "position" nor "on a scale" appears in a bank reply prompt.
A bank prompt carries no STANCE instruction and ends with the plain reply instruction, since nothing parses a bank reply for a number.
Persona, topic, lean, memory, feed, directive and the reply instruction appear in that order in a turn-1 prompt.
Every delivered post appears on its own "A user posted:" line and the count matches the feed length.
The feed lines come out in the order they were passed, since delivery order is part of the stimulus and comes from a seeded draw.
An empty feed drops the heading entirely while the reply instruction still stands. A heading with nothing under it is itself a stimulus, and a different one from no feed.
Each of the seven scale points renders its lean sentence against the run's anchor labels and contains no digit (7 cases).
A run with custom anchor labels renders the lean against those labels, so the sentence says something about the topic rather than about the scale.
Stances 1 and 7 produce leans naming the low and high anchors respectively, so the mapping is not inverted.
A stance of exactly 4 renders as undecided rather than leaning either way.
A fractional or zero initial stance from a non-7-point scale raises rather than rounding or defaulting, which would start every agent in a misconfigured run from the middle without saying so.
The memory block puts an earlier round before a later one and labels each line as read or replied.
With memory_rounds 2 and five remembered rounds, only the last two appear and there are exactly two reply lines. This is the cap that reaches the model, so it is the one that determines results.
Windows of 1, 3 and 5 each produce exactly that many reply lines from an eight-round history, so the value comes from the run rather than a constant.
An empty history drops the memory heading entirely.
The memory block contains no "Round", no agent id and no digit, since a round number would put a digit in front of the model for no benefit.
A remembered round with neither reads nor a reply produces no memory section, so a failed round spends no memory slot.
A probe prompt carries the persona, the topic, the run's question, both anchor labels against 1 and 7, and ends with the single-digit instruction.
build_probe_prompt returns a str rather than a BuiltPrompt, since a probe never carries an image.
The memory block from the reply prompt appears verbatim in the probe prompt, so the probe reads the same history the reply did.
The probe prompt asks for no reply, no STANCE line and no sentences.
The probe prompt carries no feed heading and no posted text, so the measurement is not also a stimulus.

Everything ahead of the probe question is digit-free, and the prompt mentions no position and no agent id. The digits in the anchor and instruction lines are the scale's own definition, which the model needs to answer at all.
With include_lean and no history, the probe holds persona, topic and the lean sentence, and neither a memory nor a feed section.
A builder whose run has probe_question forced to None raises rather than substituting a default, which would silently probe all four arms in English and leave no trace in the output.
Calling build_probe_prompt with no history argument produces a prompt with no memory section.

Stripping the bank-text and directive lines from an English and a Hindi prompt leaves identical line lists, and the stripped set is non-empty. So persona, topic, lean, headings and the reply instruction are byte-identical across arms.
With each arm's own directive line removed, all four arms' prompts are line-for-line identical.
A generated-regime builder still produces the position line and the STANCE contract and no bank feed, so the regime switch is what selects the path.
Passing neighbour posts and emphasize_format to a bank build produces a byte-identical prompt rather than raising, since the bank path has no stance to re-ask for.
A bank build given a meme neighbour post returns no image and no vision fallback.
Building a reply and a probe leaves the passed feed list, history list and agent stance_history unchanged.
The lean appears once in the reply prompt at turns 1, 2, 3 and 10 (4 cases).
The lean is the line straight after the topic line in every round (4 cases).
The lean survives an empty feed as well as a full one, at three turns (6 cases).
memory_rounds=None renders all seven remembered rounds, oldest first.
A config that never mentions memory_rounds keeps everything.
The probe shows the same full history the reply prompt does.
memory_rounds=2 still slices to the last two rounds, so the option remains.
A memory block with a reply and no reads renders the reply line alone.
The probe carries the lean once, with an empty history and with a full one (2 cases).
The probe puts the lean straight after the topic line, like the reply prompt.
Both calls of one round render the same lean sentence for the same agent.

groups.summary: Interval spacing, that an unconfigured provider returns immediately, that concurrent acquires for one provider serialize, and that a limit of 0 means no limit rather than a division by zero.

tests.summary: Successive acquires for one provider are separated by at least 60/limit seconds.
A provider absent from the limits dict is unlimited and returns without waiting.
Concurrent acquires for one provider serialize through its lock and stay interval-spaced.
A configured limit of 0 means no limit, rather than dividing by zero or blocking every request.
release changes no state, confirming it exists only for call-site symmetry.

groups.summary: The launcher's printed plan and its gateway wiring: the per-regime call counts including the control's, the memory line, the probe-language warning, and that launch really passes the run's max_concurrency and probe_top_logprobs through to the provider.

tests.summary: A generated run prints one line, at most M x K calls.
A bank run prints replies, probes including round 0, and the total.
The control's budget matches a treatment arm's, with no line saying "none".
The regime line describes the control as reading one side-free message.
describe() prints the neutral message in full.
The default prints as "full history", never as "None rounds".
A max_prompt_tokens ceiling appears in the memory line.
A configured window prints as "last 2 rounds".
English anchor labels in the hindi arm raise no warning.
An English probe question in the hindi arm warns, naming only that field.
The three Roman-script arms are never warned about (3 cases).
A non-default probe_top_logprobs reaches every probe call, and no reply call asks for logprobs.
launch builds the gateway with the run's max_concurrency and top_logprobs.
Unset, they pass through as None and the schema's default of 20.

groups.summary: That one seed reproduces each stream, that the three streams never correlate, that a property returns the same advancing instance, and that turn_rng is a pure function of seed, purpose and turn so a resume replays nothing.

tests.summary: Two managers built from one seed produce identical neighbour-stream draws.
The same holds for the meme-injection stream.
The three offset streams produce different sequences from the same base seed, which is what the deliberate offsets are for.
Each property returns the same object every time, not a fresh Random, so the stream can advance.
Accessing a property repeatedly keeps advancing the stream rather than restarting it.
turn_rng returns the same sequence for the same seed, purpose and turn regardless of what was drawn before, which is what makes a resumed turn identical.
Demonstrates the defect turn_rng exists to fix: a rebuilt long-lived stream replays turn 1's draws, because its position was never checkpointed.
Derived streams differ across turns and across purposes, so no two collide.
Two runs sharing a seed still draw identically from derived streams, which is what holds neighbour sampling constant while language varies.
An unknown purpose or a turn below 1 raises ValueError rather than silently producing a stream.
All four turn purposes across three turns give twelve distinct first draws, so the argument and probe offsets collide with neither each other nor the original neighbour and meme streams.

graph_seed is stable for one base seed, differs across seeds, and collides with none of the three long-lived offsets or the first 49 turns of any purpose offset. A graph built from an integer a neighbour draw consumes would correlate structure with sampling invisibly.
Two managers on the same seed give the same sender the same ten draws, with no turn in the derivation, which is what the bank's no-repeat guarantee depends on.
Changing the sender, the purpose or the seed each changes the first draw, giving four distinct values.
A purpose that is not a turn purpose, and an empty sender_id, each raise ValueError.
Inspects SeedManager.__init__ and asserts its parameters are exactly (self, seed), so there is no language, topic or trial argument for a derivation to mix in. Fails first if someone adds one.
Two managers on the same seed share a graph seed and produce identical argument draws per turn and per sender, which is what makes the four language arms the same experiment with one factor changed.

groups.summary: The widest file: per-turn row counts and neighbour shape, seeded reproducibility, meme turns costing no call, the parse-retry and fatal-error paths, cost-ceiling and unexpected-exception aborts, checkpoint intervals, resume, and that no agent sees another's same-turn output.

tests.summary: A completed run writes exactly M times K rows.
Every logged row carries exactly N neighbour ids and never the speaker's own.
A completed run leaves both agents_final.jsonl and a checkpoint on disk.
The orchestrator creates the run directory itself, which the logging writer deliberately does not do.
Turn 1 prompts carry no neighbour block, since nobody has posted yet.
Turn 2 prompts carry the neighbours' turn-1 posts.
Two runs on one seed produce identical neighbour draws throughout.
Different seeds produce different neighbour draws, confirming the seed is actually consumed.
Meme turns make no gateway call and take their stance from the dataset label, which is what makes memes a content-replacement mechanism rather than a prompt change.
A neighbour's meme arrives at a vision backend as attached image bytes.
A text-only backend records used_vision_fallback on the rows that saw a meme as caption only.
A persistently unparseable reply is retried to the budget, then logged as failed_logged_null rather than given a fabricated stance.
A reply that parses on a later attempt is logged as retried_success, so retries stay visible in the dataset.
A failed agent's stance_after repeats stance_before and no history is appended, so later turns keep reading its last known value.
A fatal gateway error fails one agent's turn and the rest of the population continues.
A fatal error produces exactly one provider call, confirming it is outside the retry policy.
A cost ceiling breach aborts the run instead of being absorbed per agent. The design doc's sample swallowed it, contradicting its own statement that it is fatal.
An unanticipated exception type propagates and aborts, so a real bug surfaces loudly rather than becoming a soft-failure row.
An abort after at least one completed turn records failed_partial, so the run does not look like it is still running.
A completed run rewrites run_config.json with status, timestamps and total cost.
Checkpoints are written on the configured interval rather than every turn.
A final turn the interval would skip is checkpointed anyway, since otherwise a completed run would resume from the wrong place.
Re-running a completed run adds no rows and makes no calls, because the checkpoint already covers turn K.
A run resumed from a mid-run checkpoint continues at the next turn rather than restarting.
A resumed run rebuilds each agent's last post from the log including its meme content, which agent state alone cannot express and which would otherwise change the stimulus mid-run.
The logged stance_before matches what the interaction engine reads. If they disagreed, every regression fitted on that column would be wrong.
Each turn's stance_before equals the previous turn's stance_after for that agent.
No prompt in a turn contains any reasoning produced in that same turn, the direct check on the frozen-snapshot guarantee that reproducibility rests on.
A failed turn is written to the log, since a failure is data rather than a gap.
A failed turn appends no StanceRecord, so no blank reasoning enters the agent's history.
Neighbours of a failed agent are shown its last real post rather than an empty contribution.

A failed turn consumes none of the agent's five memory slots. Otherwise a language condition with more parse failures would systematically receive less context, which is the asymmetry the memory cap exists to prevent.
Across three attempts the prompt is built at most twice, since only a plain and an emphasised variant exist. Rebuilding per attempt re-read the meme image from disk each time.
A completed run writes M times (K+1) rows covering turns 0 through K, with exactly M rows per turn.
Reply calls total M times K and probe calls M times (K+1), so a round is two calls per agent plus one probe each at round 0.
Every row is a bank_item with no meme id and all four probe columns populated, and every post-round-0 row carries a posted item, three items read and a reply.

Driving the probe to 4, 6, 2 then 5 across rounds, each row's stance_after is that round's reading and its stance_before is the previous round's, so stance is what the probe measured rather than anything self-reported.
Every turn-0 row has no items read, no posted item, no neighbours and no reply, but does carry a probe mean, so the starting stance is measured rather than inferred.
At K=1 there are 8 reply calls and 16 probes, so round 0 spends probes only.
A run whose first round crashes still has a checkpoint at turn 0 and only turn-0 rows, so a crash in round 1 does not cost the starting measurement and a resume cannot probe round 0 twice.
No reply or probe prompt in a whole run mentions STANCE.
Across every reply and probe prompt of a whole run, none mentions a position or contains an agent id.
With every round-0 reading at 6.0, every round-1 post is a pro item.
With every reading at 2.0, every round-1 post is a con item.

With every reading at exactly 4.0, two runs on the same seed assign identical sides and the population is genuinely split across both sides, so the tie is neither clamped to one side nor left undefined.
Each row's items_read is exactly what its listed neighbours posted that round, in neighbour order.
Every post-round-0 row lists exactly N neighbours and never the speaker itself.
Every row's neighbours are a subset of that speaker's adjacency in the strategy's own edge list.

graph_edges.csv holds the header and exactly the strategy's edges, M times degree over 2 of them. Analysis needs the structure the run used rather than one rebuilt from the config under a different networkx version.
An alpha-sampling run writes no graph_edges.csv, since there is no graph to record.

A control and a treatment arm on the same seed produce identical turn, speaker, neighbour and posted-item signatures, so every seeded stream consumes identically and the two differ only in what agents saw.
Round-1 prompts carry no memory section while round-3 prompts carry one holding two reply lines, so memory accumulates as rounds complete.
Over five rounds with a window of 2, no prompt shows more than two reply lines and at least one shows exactly two.
Every round-1 probe prompt contains the marker text the reply call returned that round, which is why Phase B runs after Phase A. That is the agent's own output, read by nobody else.
No reply prompt in the run contains a probe-only token, the probe's digit instruction or the probe question, so measuring an agent does not change what it is shown next round.
Giving every reply a unique marker, no round's reply markers appear in any prompt of that same round, which is Fix F in the bank regime.

Two runs on one seed with per-call-varying probe readings produce identical posted-item signatures. If items were resolved mid-dispatch, later agents' sides would reflect earlier agents' new readings.

When every reply call fails fatally, each round-1 row is written as failed_logged_null with an empty reply, no probe mean and stance_after equal to stance_before. No invented reply and no stance record.
With every reply failing, only the round-0 probes are spent, since the agent will not be applied this round whatever the probe says.
An off-scale round-1 probe leaves the row failed with null probe columns and an unchanged stance, while the reply text is still present: the reply happened and only the measurement failed.
With round 1's probe failing, each agent's final stance history holds turns 0 and 2 only, and round 2's prompts carry no reply lines, so the failed round spends neither a record nor a memory slot.
A fatal gateway error on every probe leaves all 16 rows written as failed_logged_null rather than aborting the run.
A RuntimeError from a reply call propagates out of the run rather than becoming a soft-failure row, since gather with return_exceptions would otherwise flatten real bugs into return values.
CostCeilingExceeded raised from a probe aborts the whole run rather than being absorbed per agent.
One failed round-0 probe leaves exactly one failed row and round 1 still runs for all 8 agents, that agent falling back to its configured initial_stance for its first side assignment.
A post-round-0 row's prompt tokens, completion tokens and latency are the sums over the reply and the probe, while a round-0 row carries the probe's figures alone.
A bank run is wired with GraphSampling and a BankManager; a default run gets AlphaSampling and no bank.
English and Hindi runs on one seed produce identical edge lists while a different seed does not, so the four arms of a trial share a structure.
Constructing a bank-regime orchestrator with bank=None raises at construction rather than on the first pick, with the run directory and config already written.
The graph's node set equals the initialized population's agent ids, since agent_id_for is shared by the wiring and by initialize_population and a drift would build a graph of non-agents.
A run crashing in round 3 leaves turns 0 to 2 logged, and a second pass completes it to turn 4.
After a crash and a resume there are exactly 8 turn-0 rows, one per agent, rather than a doubled starting measurement.
A crashed-and-resumed run and an uninterrupted one post identical items and show identical feeds, which depends on the bank cycle counts being rebuilt from the log rather than restarted.
The rebuilt post counts equal an uninterrupted run's and total M times K. Checked directly because an off-by-one would surface as a subtly different item sequence rather than as an error.

After a crash in round 3, the rebuilt history holds two rounds per agent, each with reads and a reply, and the resumed round-3 prompts carry a memory block with two reply lines. Remembered rounds cannot be checkpointed without putting post text into agent state.
After a five-round run with a window of 2, the rebuilt history holds exactly two rounds per agent.
A round whose probe failed is absent from the rebuilt history, so a resume carries the same memory an uninterrupted run would.
With every logged row duplicated on disk, the rebuilt counts still total M times K rather than twice that, keyed on (turn, speaker) with the last write kept, the same rule export_csv applies.
Re-running a finished run adds no rows and makes no further reply or probe calls.
The control makes the same M x K replies and M x (K+1) probes a treatment arm does.
Control rows read the reserved neutral id, keep the item they would have posted, and reply.
One posted line per control prompt, and no bank argument anywhere in either phase.
The control's memory block grows round over round instead of staying empty.
Control probes carry memory but never a feed: the probe measures and never delivers.
Every control probe, round 0 included, carries a whole lean sentence after the topic line.
Round 5's reply and probe prompts carry all four earlier rounds, in order.
memory_rounds=2 keeps rounds 3 and 4 and drops 1 and 2 at the orchestrator too.
An over-long reply prompt raises PromptBudgetExceeded out of the run, naming agent, round and counts.
A long probe prompt raises as well, at the round-0 probe.
A generous ceiling changes nothing: the run completes with every row.
With no ceiling, a million-token prompt is not an error.
ContextLengthExceeded propagates instead of becoming one agent's failed row.
Reply and probe prompt lengths are recorded apart, and still sum to prompt_token_count.
prompts.jsonl holds one unique line per reply and probe, with the text the model was handed.
Re-scoring each logged line's logprobs reproduces that row's probe_mean.
Logprobs are present on exactly the probe lines, so None means "not a probe".
Each reply line carries the text the gateway returned.
A fatal gateway error still logs the prompt, with an empty response.
An off-scale probe nulls its row's probe columns but still logs the distribution.
log_prompts False writes no prompts.jsonl and leaves the dataset intact.
The generated regime resolves log_prompts to False and writes no file.
A generated run that asks for prompt logging gets M x K reply lines with the STANCE contract.
A format retry logs both attempts; last-write-wins leaves the one the turn used.
A resume re-logs the uncovered round's prompts; last-write-wins recovers one per call.
A five-round run crashed in round 3 resumes with all five rounds remembered and matches a clean run row for row.
A crashed control run resumes to the same rows as an uninterrupted one.
The rebuilt control history renders the reserved id back to the neutral message.
Half a round staged on disk with no checkpoint leaves no trace in the resumed run.
A whole uncheckpointed round is ignored too, under checkpoint_every_n_turns=2.
The mechanism itself: state rebuilt as of round 1 counts round 1 only.

groups.summary: Well-formed and malformed STANCE lines, case insensitivity, negative and decimal values, that the first of several matches wins while all are stripped from reason_text, and the scale range checks.

tests.summary: A well-formed reply yields the value, and the STANCE line is removed from the reason text.
A reply with no STANCE line raises StanceParseFailure.
A non-numeric value raises StanceParseFailure.
Negative and decimal stances parse, so the pattern is not limited to positive integers.
Lower and mixed case stance labels parse.
With several STANCE substrings the first supplies the value and every one is stripped, so a restated stance cannot leak into the field the RQ2 analyses read.
An in-range value is returned unchanged, so nothing is rounded to a scale point.
A value below the scale raises rather than being clamped to the minimum.
A value above the scale raises rather than being clamped to the maximum.

groups.summary: That a vision receiver gets matching image bytes, that a text-only receiver gets the caption woven in with no image, and that the text-only path never touches the filesystem even for a nonexistent image.

tests.summary: A vision receiver gets prompt text plus the exact bytes of the file on disk.
A text-only receiver gets no image and the caption woven into the prompt text.
A missing image raises for a vision receiver, treated as a meme-pool integrity problem.
The text-only branch succeeds even when the image does not exist, proving it never reads the file.
